key: the route map pasted inside a Volvo bus
name: ch00_bus_route_map
alt: A passenger on an overnight sleeper bus studies a route map with three journey legs and a final stop marked with question marks.
scene: Interior of a long-distance overnight sleeper bus at dusk, seen from the aisle near the front. A young woman in her mid-20s, wearing a grey hoodie and holding a steel water bottle, stands on tiptoe reading a large laminated route map pasted on the partition behind the driver's cabin. The map is the hero of the picture: a winding coloured line drawn in three clear segments. The first segment is thin and twisty through small town blocks, the second is a straight thick highway with milestones, and the third ends at a big cloverleaf interchange where several highways meet. Tiny bus icons mark the stops, and a few stops are crossed out to show places the bus skips. The very last stop at the far end of the line is a dashed circle with "???" written inside it. Behind her, sleepy passengers settle into berths with blankets and earphones; the driver in a white uniform shirt adjusts the mirror; through the windscreen the road glows orange under street lamps. The woman points at the first segment with one finger, looking curious and calm rather than lost, as if she now understands where the night is heading. Warm interior reading lights, blue evening sky outside. Labels: "ROADS" under the twisty first segment, "HIGHWAY" under the straight middle segment, "INTERCHANGE" beside the cloverleaf.

key: walking into a new phone shop where
name: ch00_phone_shop_buzzwords
alt: A confused customer in a phone shop full of shouting spec banners is helped by a friend who explains the trade-offs.
scene: A bright, crowded mobile phone shop in an Indian market lane, seen from just inside the glass door. Every wall and glass counter is covered with loud starburst stickers and hanging banners shouting short spec words such as 5G, AMOLED and 120Hz, stacked over plain unbranded phone boxes. In the centre foreground a middle-aged man in a cream kurta and spectacles stands overwhelmed, holding two identical-looking phone boxes, eyebrows raised, small swirl lines around his head to show confusion. A salesman in a red polo shirt behind the counter is mid-pitch, arms spread wide. Beside the customer, his calm younger friend (late 20s, denim jacket, backpack) leans in and points at a small handwritten card she holds up, which shows a simple balance scale: on one pan a battery icon, on the other a price tag and a weight, to show that every feature costs something. Thin dotted arrows run from the noisy banners into her card, as if she is translating the noise into what it actually means. Fluorescent shop lighting, busy but friendly mood. Labels: "BUZZWORDS" across the top banner area, "TRADE-OFFS" under the balance scale on her card.

key: you queued at a counter and a clerk
name: ch00_railway_booking_pressure
alt: A quiet old railway booking counter contrasts with a flood of phones all pressing Book at exactly 10 AM.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: an old railway reservation hall with a wooden counter, steel grille and a hand-painted board; a single clerk in a white shirt and sleeve garters types slowly on a beige computer terminal while a short, orderly queue of five people waits with paper forms; a wall clock shows ten in the morning; the mood is calm and dusty. RIGHT panel: the same moment today, shown as hundreds of smartphones held up by hands from every direction, a student on a hostel bed, an auntie in a kitchen, an office worker at a desk, a farmer on a tractor, all thumbs pressing a big green book button at once; a large clock above them shows exactly 10:00; above the phones float three small weather-like icons: a rising traffic arrow, a rulebook with pages flipping, and a festival diya with a crossed-out closed sign, to stand for heavy traffic, changing rules and never being allowed to shut down. A single overloaded wire runs from all the phones back towards the old counter on the left, sparking where it meets it, showing the old one-counter design cannot carry this load. Labels: "THEN" at the top of the left panel, "NOW" at the top of the right panel.

key: Learning cricket by memorising today
name: ch00_cricket_principles
alt: One boy memorises a team list that blows away, while another learns field placements on a chalkboard that work every season.
scene: A split-panel scene at an Indian school cricket ground, late afternoon, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a teenage boy in a school uniform sits on the pavilion steps cramming a printed team-list sheet, lips moving as he memorises names; a gust of wind is already blowing several of the sheets away towards a calendar on the wall whose pages are flipping to next year, showing the lists going out of date. RIGHT panel: a girl of the same age in cricket whites and a cap stands with an old coach (60s, white moustache, tracksuit, whistle) at a green chalkboard. The coach has drawn a field diagram: a swinging ball's curved path from the bowler, and a slip fielder placed next to the keeper, with an arrow showing the edge flying to slip. A second small sketch shows a spinning pitch with cracks and a batter in a defensive stance. The girl nods with a look of real understanding, copying the diagram into a notebook. Behind them on the field, players of different teams and different jersey colours all use the same slip position, to show the idea works for any team. Golden evening light, long shadows. Labels: "BUZZWORDS" over the left panel, "PRINCIPLES" over the right panel.

key: a goods train and an oil tanker are all
name: ch00_big_vehicle_questions
alt: A mechanic ignores the label big vehicle and sorts a bus, goods train and oil tanker by two questions.
scene: A wide yard beside a highway workshop in the morning. Three very different big vehicles are parked side by side: a long passenger sleeper bus with faces at its windows, a goods train of coupled wagons on a siding, and a huge oil tanker ship visible at a dock in the background. A painted banner over all three reads "BIG VEHICLE", and it is crossed out with a thick chalk line. In the foreground an experienced mechanic in his 50s, oil-stained blue overalls, cloth on his shoulder and a spanner in hand, stands at a chalkboard on an easel. The board shows a simple two-by-two grid made by two questions drawn as small icons: one engine versus many coupled engines along the top, and a clock with waiting passengers versus a calendar with a crate along the side. He is sticking small pictures of the bus, the train and the ship into different boxes of the grid. The bus sits in the waiting-passengers row; the goods train sits in the crate row under many engines. His young helper in a cap watches, finally getting it. Clear morning light, practical mood. Labels: "ONE OR MANY" along the top of the grid, "NOW OR LATER" along the side of the grid.

key: Part I: one cook, one kitchen
name: ch00_restaurant_three_parts
alt: A three-stage picture growing from one cook in one kitchen, to a chain of branches, to a central kitchen with a live order stream.
scene: A wide illustration in three panels that read left to right like a growing business, joined by a road. PANEL ONE: a small home-style kitchen with one cook in his 30s wearing an apron, neatly labelling jars on a spice shelf and writing a recipe card in clear handwriting. PANEL TWO: five small restaurant branches in different city skylines, each with an identical menu board; delivery zones painted on the street map between them in different colours; a phone line strung between branches has a broken, sparking gap in the middle; one branch manager holds a receipt stamped either fully paid or not at all. PANEL THREE: a large central kitchen at night with giant pots of sauce being prepared in batches and stacked in crates for tomorrow, while out of its side door a constant stream of delivery riders on scooters carries single orders out into the daytime streets, drawn as a flowing river of small bags. The same cook appears in all three panels, older and in a smarter uniform each time, to show it is one learning journey. Warm, busy, optimistic mood, soft daylight. Labels: "PART I" above the first panel, "PART II" above the second, "PART III" above the third.

key: the kitchen is open, the food is good
name: ch00_soft_launch
alt: A new restaurant in its soft-launch week serves good food while a few menu items say coming soon and diners fill feedback cards.
scene: Inside a small, freshly opened restaurant with new wooden tables, potted plants and string lights, seen from a corner table at lunchtime. A paper banner over the door reads "SOFT LAUNCH". On the wall hangs a chalk menu board: most lines are filled in with dish names drawn as tiny food icons, but three lines near the bottom say "coming soon" with a small chalk clock beside each. In the foreground a family of three (a father in a checked shirt, a mother in a yellow salwar suit, a young boy) enjoy plates of hot food; the boy happily dips a dosa. The young owner, a woman in her 30s with an apron over a smart kurta and a pen behind her ear, stands at their table holding out a small feedback card and pencil with a hopeful, friendly smile; a stack of such cards sits on a little tray in her other hand. In the kitchen hatch behind her, a cook is still sticking a fresh label on a new spice jar, to show the place is open but not quite finished. Bright midday light, cheerful and slightly unfinished mood. Labels: "COMING SOON" in small chalk letters next to the unfinished menu lines, "FEEDBACK" on the card she holds out.

key: The client (the family) only talks to
name: ch01_wedding_caterer_cache
alt: A wedding caterer fronts a hidden back area with a store room, a sweets counter, a printed menu and a to-do slip box, where helpers rush to remove a finished sweet.
scene: A wedding venue cut open like a dollhouse so we see both front and back. FRONT, left side: a bride's father in a cream sherwani talks only to the head caterer, a confident man in his 40s with a white apron and a notepad, standing in front of a heavy maroon curtain. BEHIND the curtain, right side, four areas are visible: a dim store room with sacks and big steel boxes, one box marked with a sweet icon now standing empty; a bright glass sweets counter near the entrance still displaying a tray of gulab jamun; a printed menu card on a stand listing dishes as tiny icons; and a wooden box stuffed with paper to-do slips. Two young helpers in caps are mid-sprint: one runs from the empty store-room box to the sweets counter to lift the old gulab jamun tray off display, the other runs to the menu stand with a pen to strike the sweet off the list. Dotted arrows show both runs starting from the empty box. In the hall beyond, a guest is reaching for the sweet that is about to disappear. Busy, festive, slightly frantic mood under warm marigold lighting. Labels: "DATABASE" over the store room, "CACHE" over the sweets counter, "INDEX" over the menu stand.

key: Reliable: trains keep running even when
name: ch01_local_train_three_goals
alt: A suburban train network shown in three scenes: running past a failed signal, longer and more frequent trains, and engineers upgrading signals without stopping service.
scene: A busy suburban railway line in a big Indian city drawn as one long panorama split into three zones by overhead signal gantries. LEFT zone: a crowded local train glides past a signal whose lamp has gone dark, while a railway worker in an orange vest waves a green flag so the train keeps moving, and passengers hanging at the doors look unbothered. MIDDLE zone: a station platform at rush hour where a long 12-coach train arrives, with a second train already visible right behind it and a new elevated line being built in the background with cranes, showing a plan for a doubling city. RIGHT zone: a signal cabin at night where an older engineer with grey hair and reading glasses shows a young trainee a clear timetable chart on the wall, while outside two technicians on a ladder swap an old signal head for a new one as a train still passes under them. The tracks run continuously through all three zones so it reads as one network. Morning light on the left fading to evening on the right, a sense of a system that never stops. Labels: "RELIABLE" above the left zone, "SCALABLE" above the middle, "MAINTAINABLE" above the right zone.

key: A housing society with one water pump
name: ch01_water_pumps
alt: A society with one pump goes dry during servicing, a society with two pumps keeps water flowing, and a vast field of pumps routes around broken ones automatically.
scene: A three-panel scene in the pump rooms of Indian housing societies. PANEL ONE: a small pump room with a single blue electric pump opened up for servicing; a plumber in a vest kneels with tools while upstairs, through a cut-away, residents stand at dry taps holding empty buckets, one auntie frowning at the tap; a spare motor sits wrapped in plastic on a shelf. PANEL TWO: the same room with two pumps side by side; one is being serviced by the plumber, the other hums with motion lines, and the taps upstairs run happily as a girl fills a bucket, nobody upstairs even aware of the repair. PANEL THREE: a huge aerial view of rows and rows of identical pumps stretching to the horizon like a field, with pipes in a grid; a few pumps are marked with small red warning triangles, and the water flow, drawn as blue arrows, bends smoothly around them through neighbouring pumps without any person in sight, only a small control box blinking on a pole. Daylight, practical mood moving from human repair to automatic routing. Labels: "ONE PUMP" over panel one, "TWO PUMPS" over panel two, "THOUSANDS" over panel three.

key: Twelve chai stalls on a street
name: ch01_chai_stall_faults
alt: A street of twelve chai stalls shows one stall out of gas, all stalls ruined by the same spoiled milk, and a cascade of stalls closing one after another.
scene: A long street of twelve small chai stalls in a row, seen from slightly above at early morning, drawn three times as horizontal strips stacked top to bottom. TOP strip: eleven stalls steam happily with customers holding glasses, while one stall in the middle has a dead stove and an empty gas cylinder lying on its side, its owner shrugging; customers simply walk to the next stall. MIDDLE strip: a single milk van from one dairy has visited every stall, and a dotted line connects the van to all twelve stalls; every kettle now has curdled, lumpy milk with green stink lines, and every stall owner looks into his pot in dismay at the same moment. BOTTOM strip: the first stall has its shutter down; its crowd surges into the second stall, which runs out of cups and pulls its shutter halfway; the crowd moves to the third, and so on, drawn like falling dominoes with curved arrows carrying the crowd from stall to stall. Morning mist, warm yellow light, the street otherwise identical in all three strips. Labels: "HARDWARE" beside the top strip, "SYSTEMATIC" beside the middle strip, "CASCADE" beside the bottom strip.

key: app releasing a new payments screen
name: ch01_payment_app_rollout
alt: A payments team rolls out a new pay screen to a tiny slice of users while watching a failed-payments dashboard, ready to stop.
scene: A modern office room at night with a big wall screen, seen from behind a small product team. On the left a large phone mock-up on a stand shows the new pay screen: a big "PAY" button, a PIN pad, and the receiver's name shown clearly in bold above the amount. In the centre, a young developer in a hoodie tests the app on a phone filled with obviously fake toy rupee notes in a tray beside her keyboard, to show sandbox money. On the right, the wall screen shows a map of the country with a crowd of tiny people, of whom only one small cluster glows bright, to show the new screen reaching just a few users first; below it a simple line graph of failed payments per minute is flat, with a red dashed threshold line above it. A team lead in her 40s with a lanyard stands with her hand resting on a big physical red stop lever mounted on the desk, calm but alert, eyes on the graph. Coffee cups and sticky notes around. Cool screen light mixed with a warm desk lamp, focused mood. Labels: "1%" next to the glowing cluster on the map, "STOP" on the red lever.

key: the only copy of your wedding photos
name: ch01_wedding_photos_one_card
alt: A wedding photographer clutches a single memory card holding the only copy of a couple's photos, while a hackathon team happily demos from one laptop.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: the morning after a big Indian wedding, a photographer in his 30s with a camera strap round his neck sits on a sofa in a dim hotel room, holding one tiny memory card between two fingers like something precious and fragile; a glowing thought bubble above it shows hundreds of wedding moments, the varmala, the pheras, the family group shot, all squeezed into that card. On the floor his camera bag lies open, and a cup of tea is tipping towards the card, frozen just before it spills, with a worried sweat drop on his forehead. RIGHT panel: a bright college hall at a hackathon, three cheerful students in matching T-shirts gather round a single laptop on a table running a demo, pizza box and energy drink cans around; a sticky note on the laptop lid says "no backup" with a smiley face, and a judge nods. The contrast is that the left loss cannot be undone while the right is a deliberate, written-down shortcut. Soft warm light on the left, bright flat light on the right. Labels: "PRECIOUS" above the left panel, "DEMO" above the right panel.

key: Scalable to what? Twice the dine-in
name: ch01_restaurant_scalable_to_what
alt: A restaurant owner faces three kinds of growth, each hitting a different bottleneck: tables, cooking pots and the delivery packing counter.
scene: A cut-away view of a mid-sized Indian restaurant, seen like a dollhouse from the front, with the owner, a portly man in his 50s in a white shirt and gold watch, standing in the centre holding a big question-mark sign and scratching his head. Three kinds of growth press on three different parts of the building at once. On the left, the dining hall is overflowing: twice the usual families queue at the door and every table is full. In the middle, the kitchen has a single giant wedding order slip pinned up for 2,000 plates and the cooks are dwarfed by a stack of huge cooking pots, sweat on their brows. On the right, at a small packing counter by the back door, a pile of takeaway bags towers over one packer while a swarm of delivery riders on scooters waits outside under a dark sky with a clock reading nine. Each bottleneck glows with a red outline so it is clear that each kind of growth hits a different spot. Busy evening light, a little chaotic but readable. Labels: "TABLES" over the dining hall, "POTS" over the kitchen, "PACKING" over the back counter.

key: A dhobi (laundry) service vs a tea stall
name: ch01_dhobi_vs_tea_stall
alt: A laundry service measures kilos of clothes washed per day, while a tea stall customer waits with a stopwatch for one cup.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: an open-air dhobi ghat by a river at dawn, rows of washing stones and drying lines heavy with white sheets; a sturdy washerman in a folded lungi beats clothes on a stone while his helpers carry big bundles; a large weighing scale in the foreground holds a mountain of washed clothes and a chalk tally board beside it counts bundles for the day; nobody is waiting, the counter at the side is empty. RIGHT panel: a roadside tea stall at the same hour; a single office-goer in a shirt and tie stands at the counter, briefcase in one hand, looking at a large stopwatch that floats beside him with the second hand moving; the tea seller in a vest pours tea from high up into a small glass, steam rising; one long dotted arrow runs from the customer's mouth saying the order to the glass reaching his hand. The left side feels like volume and patience, the right like one person and the seconds ticking. Soft dawn light on both sides. Labels: "THROUGHPUT" above the left panel, "RESPONSE TIME" above the right panel.

key: Ordering at a busy dosa counter
name: ch01_dosa_counter_latency
alt: At a busy dosa counter, a customer's token waits in a pile before the cook makes the dosa, with small mishaps that make each wait different.
scene: A busy South Indian tiffin counter at breakfast time, seen from the customer side. In the foreground a young man in a college T-shirt holds out his hand and says his order; a long timeline arrow runs left to right along the bottom from his open mouth to the moment a hot masala dosa on a steel plate lands in his hand. Above the arrow the scene shows why the wait is long: first his paper token sits in a tall pile of tokens on a spike next to the cook, waiting its turn, then the cook, a lean man in a vest and towel on his shoulder, spreads batter on a huge black tawa for the actual making. Around the tawa, three small inset bubbles show mishaps that change the wait: the cook stepping away to answer a phone, a torn dosa being scraped off and restarted, and the tawa being scrubbed with a cloth. Other customers behind the young man hold tokens and glance at the clock. Steam, sizzling sounds drawn as squiggles, warm morning light. Labels: "WAITING" over the token pile, "SERVICE" over the tawa, "RESPONSE TIME" along the full timeline arrow.

key: for a family of six with three changes
name: ch01_ticket_counter_hol_blocking
alt: At a railway ticket counter, one person with a complicated booking holds up a long queue of people who only want platform tickets.
scene: A railway station ticket counter at ten in the morning, seen from the side so the whole queue is visible. At the window a harried father in his 40s, with a long folded paper listing six names, is leaning in and explaining three train changes to the clerk, who is typing slowly with a frown, a thick reservation chart open beside him; the father's wife and four children cluster around him with bags. Behind them stretches a long, impatient queue of ordinary people each holding just a coin or a small note for a platform ticket: a college girl checking her watch, a porter in a red shirt, an old man leaning on a umbrella, a vendor with a basket. Small clock icons float above each waiting head, getting bigger towards the back of the queue. To the right, a separate small inset shows a single man walking up to an empty counter with nobody in line, labelled as a slow one-at-a-time test that never sees any queue. Fluorescent station light, dust in the air, frustration building. Labels: "SLOW REQUEST" over the family at the window, "STUCK BEHIND" over the queue, "P99" over the very last, most irritated person.

key: one is still ironing a shirt for 30
name: ch01_family_dinner_tail
alt: A whole family waits by the car while one member is still ironing a shirt, so everyone leaves only when the slowest person is ready.
scene: An Indian family home in the evening, seen in a cut-away so we see both the driveway and an upstairs room. Outside, a family car stands with its doors open and headlights on; six family members are ready and waiting beside it, a grandmother in a shawl, a father jingling the keys, a mother with her handbag, two kids already bored and slouching against the car, and an uncle checking his watch. Each has a small tag floating above them showing a quick ready time of five minutes. Upstairs, through a lit window, a teenage son in a vest is slowly ironing a shirt on an ironing board, earphones in, completely unhurried; a big tag above him shows thirty minutes. A thick arrow runs from him down to the car, and a large clock face over the driveway is set to his time, to show the whole family leaves only when the slowest one is ready. Faint ghost outlines of extra cousins near the gate suggest that adding more people raises the odds that someone is late. Dusky blue sky, warm porch light, gently comic mood. Labels: "READY" over the waiting group, "SLOWEST" over the ironing son.

key: An Indian Railways station master
name: ch01_station_master_operability
alt: A station master works in a control room with a train position panel, logbook, procedure handbook, spare platform and a manual override lever.
scene: Inside a railway station master's cabin at dusk, seen over the shoulder of the station master, a calm woman in her 50s in a crisp white uniform with spectacles on a chain. The whole far wall is a large lit panel showing the tracks around the station as coloured lines with small glowing dots marking every train's position. On her desk: a thick open logbook with neat handwritten entries, a ring-bound handbook of standard procedures, a weather radio, and a cup of tea. To her right, mounted on the floor, a tall old-fashioned iron override lever stands next to a modern panel of automatic signal switches, and her hand rests lightly on the lever. Through the window behind her we see an older train pulling safely into platform 2 while a spare, empty platform 3 waits ready next to it. In the far distance, a shiny new high-speed train runs past an unmanned dark signal cabin with a small worried cloud over it, a subtle contrast between old trains well watched and new trains unwatched. Warm lamp light, steady confident mood. Labels: "VISIBILITY" over the wall panel, "MANUAL OVERRIDE" beside the iron lever.

key: the steering wheel, accelerator and
name: ch01_car_abstraction
alt: A driver uses simple pedals and wheel over a hidden engine, while a second messy car has its AC switch wired to the radio.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a clean cut-away view of a small family car; in the cabin a relaxed woman in her 30s drives with one hand on the steering wheel and one foot on the accelerator, smiling; below the floor, faded and greyed out like a hidden layer, sit the engine, gearbox and fuel lines, connected neatly to the pedals by tidy straight rods, so the driver never needs to look at them. RIGHT panel: the same kind of car, but its dashboard is opened up to show a rat's nest of tangled wires in every colour, taped and knotted together; the driver, a puzzled man in a checked shirt, presses the air-conditioner button and the radio display jumps to a new station at the same time, music notes flying out; a thick dotted arrow runs from the AC button through the tangle straight into the radio. A roll of tape and a pair of pliers lie on the passenger seat. Clean daylight on the left, slightly gloomy garage light on the right. Labels: "ABSTRACTION" above the left panel, "BIG BALL OF MUD" above the right panel.

key: Changing the menu of a busy restaurant
name: ch01_kitchen_evolvability
alt: A restaurant switches from cooking every order fresh to prepping sauces in the morning while still serving guests, with the storeroom and staff routine changing too.
scene: A cut-away of a busy restaurant kitchen shown as a before and after, separated by a thin vertical line but sharing the same dining room at the front, where guests keep eating the whole time. LEFT half, labelled with a small sun at high noon: every cook stands at his own stove making each order from scratch, chopping onions, frying spices, a ticket rail crowded with orders above them. RIGHT half, with a small rising-sun icon for early morning: the same cooks stand around big pots preparing sauces in bulk; the storeroom shelves behind them have been rearranged with new labelled tubs of sauce; a shift timetable on the wall shows a new early-morning slot; at the pass, a cook simply ladles sauce over grilled items so plates go out fast. A smiling head chef in his 40s with a tall white hat walks through the doorway between the two halves carrying a tub, connecting them. In the small dining room in front, a waiter serves a family without any interruption, a sign on the door saying "OPEN" in both halves. Warm kitchen light, steam, efficient mood. Labels: "COOK FRESH" over the left kitchen, "PREP SAUCES" over the right kitchen.

key: A file folder per person (document)
name: ch02_three_family_records
alt: The same family facts kept three ways: a folder per person, ruled registers matched by number, and a family tree of strings on a wall.
scene: A warm living room of an Indian home, seen straight on, divided into three zones along one long wall. LEFT zone: a steel almirah with its door open, holding a neat row of fat cardboard file folders, one per family member, each with a small photo clipped to its spine; a grandson pulls out the folder with grandmother's photo and everything about her spills out at once, her certificates, ration card and old letters. MIDDLE zone: on a wooden desk lie two long ruled registers side by side, one listing people and one listing addresses; a careful uncle with reading glasses runs a finger along a matching serial number in both registers, with a thin dotted line joining the two rows. RIGHT zone: on the wall, a big hand-drawn family tree made of photos pinned to a board and joined by coloured strings that cross freely, cousins to in-laws to a small sketched village, some strings looping across the whole board; a curious teenage girl follows one string with her finger. The same faces appear in all three zones, to show the same facts stored three ways. Soft afternoon light, homely mood. Labels: "DOCUMENT" above the folders, "RELATIONAL" above the registers, "GRAPH" above the string board.

key: The app turns that into an order record
name: ch02_dosa_order_layers
alt: A dosa order passes down four layers, from a hungry customer's thought to an order record, a kitchen ticket and heat on thermal paper.
scene: A tall vertical cross-section drawn like a four-storey building, each floor a different layer, connected by a single glowing arrow running straight down through all four. TOP floor: a young woman in a yellow T-shirt lounges on a sofa holding her phone, a thought bubble showing a crispy masala dosa. SECOND floor: a clean grid of boxes like a form, holding small icons for dosa, quantity, address and payment, neatly filled in. THIRD floor: a restaurant kitchen where a cook in a cap glances at a small printed ticket clipped above the stove, the dosa icon now just a short line of print. BOTTOM floor: a close-up of a little thermal printer, its tiny heating head pressing on a roll of shiny paper, with small red heat waves and a magnifier showing dark dots being burned into the paper. Each floor's character looks only at their own floor and never up or down: the woman never sees the printer, the printer never sees the dosa. Bright, clean, clean, orderly composition with warm colours. Labels: "LAYER 1" beside the top floor, "LAYER 4" beside the bottom floor.

key: fancy new lunch box with a gimmick
name: ch02_steel_tiffin_wins
alt: Fancy gimmick lunch boxes trend and are abandoned while office workers keep coming back to the plain steel tiffin.
scene: An office pantry table at lunchtime, seen from slightly above. In the centre sits a plain, dented, shining stacked steel tiffin with three tiers and a clip handle, slightly worn but clearly well loved. Around it, in a semicircle, lie a series of flashy gimmick lunch boxes from different years: a neon box with a built-in fan, a box shaped like a rocket, a box with a tiny screen, a heated electric box with a tangled cord, each with a small faded sticker of a rising trend arrow, and most of them pushed aside, cracked or gathering dust. A timeline ribbon runs along the bottom edge of the table showing the years passing. Several office workers of different ages, a young intern, a manager in a tie, a woman in a sari, all reach past the fancy boxes for their own identical steel tiffins, opening them to show rice, dal and sabzi. One young man looks guiltily at his abandoned rocket box. A few useful ideas from the gimmick boxes, like a small attached spoon, are shown clipped onto the steel tiffin's side. Bright midday light, gently humorous mood. Labels: "RELATIONAL" on a tag tied to the steel tiffin, "TRENDS" along the timeline ribbon.

key: A kitchen has a pressure cooker, a tawa
name: ch02_kitchen_utensils_polyglot
alt: A home cook uses a pressure cooker for rice, a tawa for dosa and a kadai for frying, each utensil for its own dish.
scene: A compact Indian home kitchen with a two-burner gas stove and a granite counter, seen from the front at dinner prep time. A cheerful middle-aged woman in a cotton sari with an apron, hair in a bun, works three utensils at once. On the left burner, a pressure cooker whistles with a puff of steam, rice visible through a cut-away inside it. On the right burner, a flat black tawa holds a golden dosa that she is flipping with a steel spatula. On a portable third burner on the counter, a deep iron kadai bubbles with oil and puffing puris. Each utensil has a small speech-bubble-like tag showing the one dish it is best at. Above the stove, a shelf holds jars and a small family photo. In the background a nephew peeks in, holding a cookbook titled with a big question mark, as if asking which one is the real utensil, and she laughs and gestures at all three. A thin line connects the three dishes to one dinner plate on the counter, where they come together. Warm evening kitchen light, steam curling up. Labels: "RICE" by the cooker, "DOSA" by the tawa, "FRYING" by the kadai.

key: the dialer and UPI all show that one
name: ch02_contact_id_vs_copy
alt: One saved contact entry feeds three phone apps that show the same new photo, while copies kept separately go stale.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing a large smartphone floating in the middle with three small app windows around it. LEFT panel: in the centre of the phone sits a single contact card with a smiling grandmother's photo and an ID number badge; three thin glowing lines run from that one card out to three app windows, a dialer, a chat app and a payments app, and all three show the same new photo of her wearing a green sari. A young man's thumb has just tapped "edit" on the central card. RIGHT panel: the same phone, but now each of the three app windows keeps its own separate little copy of her card in its own pocket; the young man has updated only the chat app's copy to the green-sari photo, while the dialer and payments windows still show an old photo of her in a blue sari, slightly faded with a dusty look and a small clock icon to show they are stale. Above the right phone a puzzled face of the young man appears. Clean, bright, simple background. Labels: "ONE ID" over the central card on the left, "COPIES" over the three separate cards on the right.

key: drawn as a strict tree: each person
name: ch02_strict_tree_daughter_in_law
alt: On a strict family tree, a daughter-in-law who belongs to two branches must be drawn twice or replaced with a see-page-4 note.
scene: A large paper family tree pinned to a wall, drawn in neat hanging branches where every person hangs under exactly one parent, like an upside-down tree. On the left side is the husband's family branch; on the far right is another family's branch. A young bride in a red and gold wedding sari steps forward between them, holding hands with her husband who is drawn on the left branch, while her own parents on the right branch hold her other hand. An elderly grandfather in a dhoti and spectacles stands below with a pen, puzzled about where to draw her. Two solutions are shown. On the left branch, he has pasted a second, slightly faded photocopy of her photo, making a duplicate. On the right branch, instead of her photo there is a small sticky note reading "see page 4" with an arrow curling off the edge of the chart. A strained, twisted string between the two places shows that the strict tree cannot hold one person in two places. Warm interior light, gentle confusion rather than conflict. Labels: "DUPLICATE" by the photocopied photo, "REFERENCE" by the sticky note.

key: the pickle is shared from a big jar
name: ch02_shared_pickle_jar
alt: Diners with compartment tiffins and diners with plates all reach for the same shared mango pickle jar on the table.
scene: A long dining table in an office canteen, seen from the side at lunchtime. On the left side sit three workers each eating from a compartment tiffin, rice, dal and sabzi neatly in their own separate sections, everything they need packed together. On the right side sit three other workers eating from flat steel plates served from the canteen counter. In the exact middle of the table stands one big ceramic pickle jar with a cloth tied over its mouth and a handwritten label tag showing a mango. Hands from both sides, a man in a striped shirt from the tiffin side and a woman with bangles from the plate side, reach for the same jar at once with spoons; dotted arrows from each person's food point to the one jar to show both kinds of meal share it by name. A small inset bubble near the jar shows a tiny delay clock to hint that reaching across costs a moment. Bright canteen light, friendly lunchtime chatter drawn as small squiggles. Labels: "DOCUMENT" above the tiffin side, "RELATIONAL" above the plate side, "SHARED" on the pickle jar.

key: Choosing between a ready-made thali
name: ch02_thali_vs_a_la_carte
alt: One table gets identical ready thalis while another mixes and shares separately ordered dishes.
scene: A split view of a busy family restaurant at dinner time, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT side: a table of four office colleagues in similar formal shirts each has an identical large steel thali with small bowls arranged in a circle, dal, sabzi, rice, roti and a sweet, all served in one go by a waiter carrying a stack of matching thalis; everyone eats the same set meal quickly and happily. RIGHT side: a big joint family at a round table orders dishes one by one from a menu; bowls of paneer, dal makhani, biryani and naan arrive separately and sit in the middle on a lazy Susan; hands reach across to share and mix, a child takes biryani with a spoon of raita, a grandmother adds dal to her rice, and the menu card is covered with ticks. A waiter writes new orders on a notepad. A small chalkboard by the kitchen door lists the fixed thali on one side and a long list of separate dishes on the other. Warm yellow lamps, cheerful atmosphere, the left side tidy and uniform, the right side lively and combinatorial. Labels: "THALI" above the left table, "A LA CARTE" above the right table.

key: A courier parcel vs. a library
name: ch02_parcel_vs_library
alt: A sealed courier box holds one complete order, while a library catalogue drawer cross-references authors, books and members.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a courier dispatch counter where a young packer in a uniform cap seals one brown cardboard box with tape; through a cut-away in the box we see one customer's complete order inside, a book, a shirt and a mug, with the customer's address label on the lid; a neat stack of identical sealed boxes waits for the delivery van. The scene feels simple: one box, one customer, ship and done. RIGHT panel: a quiet old college library with tall wooden card-catalogue drawers; an elderly librarian in a cardigan has pulled out a long drawer full of index cards, and coloured threads run from cards to shelves, from an author's card to several books, from books to member cards, and from member cards to a college badge pinned on the wall. A curious student leans in, asking which books by one author are borrowed by members of one college, and the librarian follows the threads with her finger. Warm wooden tones on the right, brisk practical light on the left. Labels: "ONE BOX" over the courier box, "CROSS-REFERENCE" over the catalogue drawer.

key: refuses to submit without age and berth
name: ch02_form_vs_notebook_schema
alt: A strict railway reservation form rejects a missing field, while a shopkeeper's notebook accepts any scribble and a later reader is puzzled.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a railway reservation office; a young traveller in a backpack holds a pink printed reservation form with clearly ruled boxes for name, age and berth preference; the age box is empty, and the stern clerk behind the window pushes the form back with a big red rubber stamp mark showing a cross; every accepted form in the tray beside the clerk has every box filled. RIGHT panel: a small kirana shop counter; a cheerful shopkeeper in a vest hands a pen to a customer who scribbles freely in a battered spiral notebook, numbers and words at odd angles, some circled, some crossed out; months later, shown as a small inset bubble, the shopkeeper's son sits at the same counter squinting at one scribbled number with a big question mark over his head, unsure if it is a phone number or an amount owed. The left side feels strict and orderly, the right relaxed and messy. Daylight in both. Labels: "SCHEMA-ON-WRITE" above the left panel, "SCHEMA-ON-READ" above the right panel.

key: packs a monthly ration bag for you
name: ch02_ration_bag_locality
alt: A kirana shopkeeper hands over a heavy monthly ration bag in one trip, but a customer who wants only salt must lift the whole bag.
scene: Inside a small neighbourhood kirana shop with shelves of packets, sacks of rice and a weighing scale on the counter. The shopkeeper, a friendly man in his 50s with a moustache and a white vest, lifts one huge stuffed cloth ration bag onto the counter, its top open to show atta, dal, oil bottle, sugar and a small packet of salt tucked inside, everything for a month in one place on one shelf. On the left, a happy customer, a mother with a shopping trolley, grabs the whole bag in one trip with a smile. On the right, a thin old man who only wanted the salt strains comically to lift the entire 20 kilo bag, knees bending, a tiny packet of salt visible inside, sweat drops flying. Behind the counter, a shop boy is unpacking and repacking a second bag because one more item, a big jar, does not fit, with items spread out all over the counter. A small tag on the bag shows the weight. Warm tube-light glow, gently comic mood. Labels: "ONE TRIP" over the mother with the bag, "WHOLE BAG" over the old man straining.

key: phones added better cameras, cameras
name: ch02_phone_camera_converge
alt: A smartphone and a camera borrow features from each other and merge into one hybrid device, while a specialist camera still stands aside.
scene: A simple, playful scene on a clean light background. On the left stands a friendly smartphone with little arms and legs; on the right, a chunky camera with arms and legs. They walk towards each other along a curved path. The phone is reaching over and taking a big zoom lens from the camera and clipping it onto its own back, while the camera is taking a small Wi-Fi symbol and a row of tiny app icons from the phone and sticking them onto its own side. Small swap arrows loop between them. In the middle, where their paths meet, they merge into a single hybrid device held up by a smiling young woman in a kurta, who is photographing a festival scene with it. Off to the side, on a tripod on a hill, a professional wildlife photographer in a khaki vest keeps using a huge specialist camera with a long telephoto lens to shoot a distant bird, to show the specialist tool still has its place. Bright, friendly daylight. Labels: "RELATIONAL" above the phone, "DOCUMENT" above the camera, "HYBRID" under the merged device.

key: one paneer tikka, less spicy
name: ch02_order_vs_recipe
alt: A diner states what she wants and the kitchen decides how, while a home cook follows a fixed step-by-step recipe on one stove.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a restaurant table where a young woman in a denim jacket tells a waiter her order, with a speech bubble showing a plate of paneer tikka and a chilli icon crossed half out for less spicy; behind a swinging kitchen door, a busy kitchen decides everything: a head cook points to one of two glowing clay tandoors, a newly installed second tandoor is shining with a ribbon still on it, and two cooks work in parallel, so her order comes out faster without her saying anything new. RIGHT panel: a small home kitchen where a man in his 30s in a T-shirt follows a long handwritten recipe card taped to the wall with numbered steps 1, 2, 3; he does every step himself on one stove; a second stove stands unused beside him, and to use it he would have to rewrite the recipe card, shown by an eraser and pencil resting on the card. Warm kitchen lights, the left feeling relaxed and the right effortful. Labels: "DECLARATIVE" above the left panel, "IMPERATIVE" above the right panel.

key: the class monitor wears a badge
name: ch02_monitor_badge_rule
alt: A classroom rule automatically follows the new monitor, while a badge pinned by hand stays on the old monitor.
scene: An Indian school classroom with wooden benches and a green chalkboard, seen from the back of the room. The chalkboard has a simple rule drawn as a picture: a badge icon with an arrow pointing to the word monitor in a speech-style box. A split down the middle of the room shows two outcomes. LEFT half: the new class monitor, a confident girl with two plaits in a blue uniform, stands at the front, and a soft glowing badge appears on her chest by itself, linked to the chalkboard rule by a dotted golden line; the former monitor, a boy, sits back at his bench with no badge. RIGHT half: the same classroom, but a teacher in a sari had pinned a real metal badge on the boy on Monday; it is now Thursday by the desk calendar, the girl is monitor, and yet the boy still wears the pinned badge proudly while the girl stands without one, looking at it with a frown; the teacher is busy grading papers and has not noticed. Morning sunlight through tall windows. Labels: "RULE" on the chalkboard, "PINNED" by the boy's badge in the right half.

key: Stations are vertices, tracks are edges
name: ch02_railway_map_graph
alt: A big wall railway map with stations as dots and tracks as lines, with passengers and trains added as more dots joined by lines.
scene: A large old-style railway map of India on the wall of a station waiting room, the map hand-painted with stations as round dots and tracks as lines that branch and cross. A traveller in his 40s with a trolley bag and a sleeveless jacket traces a glowing path with his finger from a western city dot to a far north-eastern city dot, the route lighting up through several junctions in between, and small hop counters appear at each junction to show nobody knew in advance how many hops it would take. On top of the map, in a slightly different colour, extra small round pins have been added: little passenger figures and little train icons, connected by thread to stations and to each other, so a booking links a passenger to a train and the train to the stations it passes through. One central-India junction dot glows, and threads lead from it back through trains to the passenger pins that booked them. A porter in a red shirt and a small child watch with interest. Warm waiting-room light, ceiling fan, wooden benches. Labels: "VERTEX" beside a station dot, "EDGE" along a track line.

key: NRIs from Kerala now living in the Gulf
name: ch02_alumni_forward_backward
alt: Two clerks search an alumni directory two ways: one checks every person, the other starts from a short list of places and looks up who links to them.
scene: A college alumni office with tall shelves of thick directories, seen from the front. Two clerks sit at desks side by side, racing to answer the same question written on a slip pinned between them, drawn as a palm-tree coastline icon with an arrow to a desert skyline icon. LEFT desk: a tired young clerk in a checked shirt works through a towering stack of alumni cards one by one, checking each card's hometown stamp and current-city stamp, the stack enormous and his finished pile tiny. RIGHT desk: an experienced woman clerk in her 50s with glasses on a chain has instead written two short lists on a notepad, the coastal towns on one side and the desert cities on the other, and is now pulling only the few cards linked to those places by coloured tags from an index box; her finished pile is already done. A wall clock above them shows how long each has taken. Both arrive at the same small set of alumni photos in the end, pinned on a board between them. Calm office lighting, a gentle race. Labels: "FORWARD" above the left desk, "BACKWARD" above the right desk.

key: Round 1: you. Round 2: everyone you
name: ch02_family_contacts_rings
alt: A family's phone contacts spread out in rings like ripples, each round adding new people until a round adds nobody new.
scene: A top-down view of a big open courtyard at a family gathering, with people standing in concentric rings like ripples on a pond. In the exact centre stands a young woman in a kurta holding up her phone. Ring two, close around her, holds her saved contacts, parents, siblings and best friends, each joined to her by a thin glowing line from her phone. Ring three, further out, holds uncles, aunts and cousins, each linked by lines from someone in ring two. Ring four holds distant relatives, linked again from ring three. Some lines loop back inward to people already in an inner ring, and those people are drawn with a small faint tick mark to show they are not counted twice. At the very outer edge, a final ring is drawn as an empty dashed circle with no new people in it, and a small stop sign sits on it. Numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 mark the rounds near the rings. Warm late-afternoon sunlight, festive strings of marigolds overhead. Labels: "ROUND 1" by the centre, "NO NEW NAMES" on the empty outer ring.

key: A cricket scorecard written as one-line
name: ch02_cricket_fact_triples
alt: A scorer writes a match as small three-part fact strips on a board, linking players, runs and teams.
scene: A cricket pavilion's scorer's box with a large corkboard on the wall, seen from inside. A scorer in his 60s with a white cap and spectacles is pinning up small paper strips, each strip divided into three coloured parts: a subject, a verb and an object. The subjects and objects are drawn as small portrait cards of generic players in team jerseys or as plain number tags. One strip links a batter card to a verb showing a bat hitting a ball and to a number tag; another strip links that same batter card to a verb showing a catch and to a fielder card; a third links the fielder card to a verb showing a flag and to a team crest card. Coloured threads connect matching cards across strips, so together the strips build up the whole match like a web. Through the window behind him a live match is in play on a green field under floodlights. A young assistant hands him a fresh blank strip. Warm interior lamp light, tidy, absorbed mood. Labels: "SUBJECT" above the first part of a strip, "PREDICATE" above the middle part, "OBJECT" above the last part.

key: Two companies both have an employee
name: ch02_grade_prefix_collision
alt: Two offices' files both have a column called grade with different meanings, and prefix tags keep them apart when merged.
scene: A meeting room where two office teams are merging their paper files onto one long table. On the left stands an HR manager in a blazer holding a file whose column header shows grade with a small salary-band icon of stacked coins. On the right stands a school examiner in a cardigan holding a file whose column header also shows grade but with an exam-marks icon of a pencil and an answer sheet. In the middle of the table, an earlier attempt to combine the files has made a mess: papers jumbled, coins mixed with answer sheets, a coffee cup knocked over, and a junior clerk holding his head. To the right of the mess, the same clerk now calmly sticks small coloured prefix tags onto each header before merging, a blue tag for the company and a green tag for the school, and the merged stack beside him is tidy with both kinds of grade side by side, never confused. Bright office light, the mess drawn with slight comic chaos. Labels: "COMPANY" on the blue prefix tag, "SCHOOL" on the green prefix tag.

key: Working out relatives at a wedding
name: ch02_wedding_rules_datalog
alt: At a wedding, two simple rules applied again and again fill in a family tree generation by generation without anyone writing a loop.
scene: A wedding hall decorated with marigold strings, with a big family tree board set up near the entrance on an easel. Two simple rules are written on two small brass plaques at the top of the board, shown as pictures: one shows a person standing inside a family circle, the other shows a child holding a parent's hand with an arrow pulling the child into the parent's circle. On the board, the tree fills in like a wave from the top down: the eldest generation already has photos glowing gold, the next generation is lighting up as the second rule is applied, shown by small sparkles and arrows, and the bottom generation is still grey, waiting for the next round. Small round number badges 1, 2, 3 show the rounds. Guests in bright saris and kurtas cluster around the board, an aunt pointing out a cousin, a child finding her own photo. In the background the same circles reappear on a seating plan and a gift list pinned on another board, showing the rule is reused. Festive warm lights. Labels: "RULE 1" on the first plaque, "RULE 2" on the second plaque.

key: keeps every item in a neat sorted shelf
name: ch03_two_kirana_shops
alt: One kirana owner tidies a perfectly sorted shelf and finds items instantly, while another dumps new stock at the front and searches slowly.
scene: A split-panel illustration of two neighbouring kirana shops on the same street, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT shop: the owner, a neat man in his 40s with a pencil behind his ear, is slowly placing a just-delivered carton of biscuits into exactly the right gap on a perfectly sorted wall of shelves, every packet in labelled rows; a delivery boy waits impatiently with more cartons, tapping his foot; but in a small inset, a customer asks for a soap and the owner reaches it in one quick move without looking. RIGHT shop: the owner, a relaxed younger man in a T-shirt, simply heaps every new delivery in a big pile near the front door, unloading a carton in seconds while the delivery boy smiles and leaves early; in the matching inset, a customer asks for a soap and the owner is half-buried in the pile, digging with both arms, packets flying. A small clock beside each inset shows how long each search takes. Bright midday street light, gently comic contrast. Labels: "SLOW WRITE, FAST READ" above the left shop, "FAST WRITE, SLOW READ" above the right shop.

key: plus an extra sheet sorted by surname
name: ch03_register_extra_sheets
alt: A teacher finds a student fast using an extra sheet sorted by surname, but must write every new student into three sheets.
scene: A school staff room with a long wooden table, seen from the side. A teacher in her 30s in a cotton sari and spectacles sits with three open ledgers in front of her: the main attendance register sorted by roll number, a second thinner sheet sorted by surname, and a third sheet sorted by house colour with small red, blue, green and yellow flag icons in the margin. On the left side of the picture, a parent asks for a student by surname, and the teacher finds him instantly by running a finger down the surname sheet, a quick arrow jumping straight to the right line. On the right side, a new student, a small boy with an oversized school bag, stands at her elbow with his admission slip, and she is busily writing his name three times, once in each sheet, with three curved arrows from his slip to the three books and a pile of more admission slips waiting. Ink bottle, pens and a bell on the table. Warm morning light through a window. Labels: "INDEX" above the surname sheet, "3 WRITES" next to the three arrows from the new student's slip.

key: A dabbawala's sorting sheet. The tiffins
name: ch03_tiffin_rack_slot_sheet
alt: Tiffins sit on a long rack in arrival order, and a sorter's sheet maps each office to the slot of its latest tiffin.
scene: A railway station platform at mid-morning where a long wooden rack holds a row of round tiffin carriers in numbered slots, in the order they arrived, slot 1 on the far left to the newest slot on the far right. A tiffin sorter in a white kurta and a white cap holds a small clipboard sheet with two columns, office numbers and slot numbers, and one line shows an office number pointing to a slot number. From that line a bold arrow jumps straight down the rack to the matching tiffin, and the sorter walks directly to it without checking any others. At the far right end of the rack, a newly arrived tiffin for the same office is being placed in the last slot by a young helper, and the sorter's pencil is crossing out the old slot number on the sheet and writing the new one; the old tiffin further down is shown greyed out. A thought bubble over the sorter's head shows a tiny copy of the same sheet, to show he keeps it in his head. Morning sunlight, trains in the background. Labels: "LOG" along the rack, "HASH MAP" on the clipboard sheet.

key: Every so often an assistant copies the
name: ch03_scorer_compaction
alt: A cricket scorer keeps writing every run on new lines while an assistant copies old pages into a clean summary of latest scores and tears the old pages out.
scene: A cricket scorer's box at a club ground, seen from inside through a long window onto the field. On the left, the main scorer, a man in his 50s with a cap and a pencil, writes nonstop in an open notebook, each new run on a fresh line under the last, the same batter's name repeating with a growing number; a filled page is being flipped and a fresh page begun. On the right, at a separate small table, his young assistant in a club sweater works quietly on older pages: she reads through two stacked full pages, copies only the latest score for each batter onto one clean summary card, and tears the old pages out, dropping them in a wastepaper basket. A curved arrow runs from the old pages through her hands into the summary card. The scorer does not look up or pause while she works, shown by motion lines on his pencil. Outside, a batter hits the ball and the umpire signals. Afternoon light, steady, quiet concentration. Labels: "APPEND" above the scorer's notebook, "COMPACTION" above the assistant's table.

key: When the register is recopied, both
name: ch03_tombstone_and_checksum
alt: A railway clerk adds a cancelled line instead of tearing out an old booking, and a bill with a total reveals a page torn mid-writing.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a railway booking clerk in a white shirt and sleeve garters sits at a wooden desk with a thick bound register; an old line for one booking is still there, and below it he is stamping a brand-new line with a big red rubber stamp that leaves a bold cancelled mark; a small grave-stone shaped icon floats above the stamp to hint at the name. In an inset bubble, the register is later being recopied into a fresh book, and both the old booking line and the cancel line are left out, crossed through with a pencil. RIGHT panel: a shop counter where a handwritten bill on a long paper slip lists items and prices with a total underlined at the bottom; the bottom half of the slip is torn off jaggedly mid-line, and the shopkeeper adds the remaining numbers on a small calculator that shows a different total, with a red exclamation mark. Warm desk lamps, careful mood. Labels: "TOMBSTONE" above the left panel, "CHECKSUM" above the right panel.

key: A hash map is like a cloakroom
name: ch03_cloakroom_vs_shelf
alt: A cloakroom attendant fetches one coat instantly but must look up a range of tokens one by one, while a library shelf lets you walk through a range in order.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a theatre cloakroom with rows of hooks; coats and shawls hang in scattered positions with numbered tokens dangling from them in no particular order, number 42 next to number 7 next to number 31. A smiling attendant in a waistcoat instantly lifts down coat 42 for a guest holding token 42, a short straight arrow from token to hook. Behind the guest, another guest holds a long list asking for all tokens from 20 to 45, and the attendant now runs back and forth to many scattered hooks, many zigzag arrows tangling across the rack, sweating. RIGHT panel: a calm library aisle with a long shelf of books arranged in strict numeric order on their spines; a student walks along the shelf from the first book in her range, lifting each next book in a single smooth sweep until she passes the last one, a single straight arrow running along the shelf. Soft warm light on both sides. Labels: "HASH" above the cloakroom, "SORTED" above the library shelf.

key: the guide words at the top of each page
name: ch03_dictionary_and_merge
alt: Guide words at the top of dictionary pages act as a sparse index, and a teacher merges three alphabetical class lists by always taking the smallest name.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a close-up of a thick English dictionary lying open on a wooden desk; the guide words printed at the top corners of the two pages are highlighted with a yellow marker, and a young student's finger lands on the right page first, then slides down just a few lines to the word she wants; tabs on the dictionary's edge show only a few markers, not one per word. RIGHT panel: a teacher in a cardigan sits at a staff-room table with three short stacks of name cards, each stack already alphabetical; she looks at the three top cards, picks the one that comes first alphabetically, and places it on a single growing merged pile in front of her; a curved arrow runs from the top of each of the three stacks into the one merged pile, with the smallest one highlighted. A pencil, a mug of tea and a stapler sit nearby. Calm study light, orderly mood. Labels: "SPARSE INDEX" above the dictionary page, "MERGE" above the teacher's merged pile.

key: A Bloom filter is a watchman at a
name: ch03_watchman_bloom_filter
alt: A society gate watchman checks three tick boxes per name and turns away a visitor at once when any box for that name is blank.
scene: The gate of a big Indian housing society in the evening, seen from the visitor's side. A watchman in his 50s in a khaki uniform and cap sits in a small glass cabin with a large printed sheet of numbered tick boxes on his desk, about thirty boxes in rows, some ticked with a pen and some blank. A visitor in a polo shirt stands at the window holding a box of sweets and says a name. Three thin lines run from the visitor's name bubble to exactly three boxes on the sheet, chosen by a little rule card pinned beside it. One of the three boxes is blank and glows red, so the watchman confidently shakes his head and raises a hand without getting up. In a small inset bubble on the right, a second visitor's name lands on three boxes that are all ticked, and the watchman gets up with a torch to walk into the tower blocks to check, a question mark over him because the ticks might have been made by other residents. Tower blocks with lit windows behind. Blue evening light, a single lamp in the cabin. Labels: "DEFINITELY NOT" by the red blank box, "MAYBE" over the inset.

key: Three hops, even for a billion PNRs
name: ch03_pnr_zone_desks_btree
alt: A railway enquiry hall works like a tree: a root signboard sends you to a zone desk, which sends you to one counter holding the booking.
scene: A large railway enquiry hall drawn as a three-level tree that reads from top to bottom. TOP: a big signboard hanging from the ceiling with a few wide number ranges, each with an arrow pointing to a different zone desk below. MIDDLE: a row of four zone desks, each staffed by a clerk with a smaller signboard of narrower ranges, each range pointing down to one of many small counters. BOTTOM: a long row of counters, each with a clerk and a filing tray of booking slips. A passenger in a sweater holding a printed ticket follows a highlighted path: under the top sign, to one zone desk, then to counter 3, where the clerk hands back his booking, three hops in total marked with small numbered footprints. To one side, one counter is overflowing with slips and a queue; a clerk is carrying half of its files to a brand-new empty counter next to it, while a worker on a ladder adds one new line to the zone desk's signboard. Bright hall lighting, orderly crowd. Labels: "ROOT" on the top signboard, "LEAF" over the row of counters, "SPLIT" by the clerk carrying half the files.

key: A bank cashier updating three passbooks
name: ch03_cashier_daybook_wal
alt: A bank cashier first writes a transfer in a day-book before updating passbooks, then after a power cut uses the day-book to finish the job.
scene: A small bank branch cash counter at evening, shown in two moments side by side, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT moment: a careful cashier in her 40s with glasses and a cardigan writes one transfer into a big day-book first, then reaches for three passbooks on the counter to update them; she has updated two, with green ticks over them, when the lights go out, a jagged lightning icon over the ceiling fan and the third passbook still open and unchanged. A small sign on the counter flipped to closed shows she has stopped anyone reading the passbooks mid-change. RIGHT moment: power is back, the fan spins, and she sits with the day-book open, finger on the last entry, calmly finishing the third passbook, all three now with green ticks; a curved arrow runs from the day-book entry to the third passbook. A customer waits patiently behind the glass. Warm tube-light glow returning on the right, darkness with a candle on the left. Labels: "WRITE-AHEAD LOG" over the day-book, "LATCH" on the small closed sign.

key: Copy-on-write is like correcting an
name: ch03_new_card_copy_on_write
alt: Instead of erasing an old ID card, a new card with the new address is issued and the records pointer moves to it, while someone holding the old card still sees the old address.
scene: A government enrolment office with a counter and a big wall cabinet of index slots. A young woman in a salwar suit has just moved house; the officer, a man in his 40s with a moustache, hands her a freshly printed national ID card showing a new house icon and a new address line, while her old card, showing an old house icon, is not shredded but stays on the counter intact. On the wall behind, a single big arrow on a pivot, like a railway signal, has just swung from pointing at a slot holding the old card to pointing at a slot holding the new card, a small motion trail showing the swing. In the foreground on the left, a courier man still holds a photocopy of her old card and reads the old address happily, unaware, showing that anyone holding the old copy sees the old version. A small inset in the upper right shows a phone-book page header with just two short letters on it, beside a long full name squashed out, to hint at abbreviated keys. Neutral office light. Labels: "OLD" over the old card, "NEW" over the new card.

key: A clustered index is a shelf where the
name: ch03_catalogue_card_indexes
alt: A library shows a catalogue card pointing to a shelf slot, a shelf already in catalogue order, a card that answers the question itself, and a moved-to note on an empty slot.
scene: An old public library interior with tall wooden shelves and a card-catalogue cabinet, arranged as four small vignettes around a central reader. TOP LEFT: a student pulls a catalogue card that shows a shelf number and slot number, and a dotted arrow leads from the card across the room to a distant shelf where the book sits. TOP RIGHT: a shelf where the books themselves stand in exact catalogue order, so the librarian finds the card and the book in the same spot, the card tucked right in front of the book. BOTTOM LEFT: a reader holds a fatter catalogue card that already lists the author's name and the year, and she smiles and puts the card back without walking to any shelf at all. BOTTOM RIGHT: an empty slot on a shelf with a small handwritten note pinned to it showing an arrow and a different shelf number. In the middle, an elderly librarian in a cardigan and spectacles points to each vignette. Warm wood tones, dust in sunbeams. Labels: "NONCLUSTERED" over the top-left, "CLUSTERED" over the top-right, "COVERING" over the bottom-left vignette.

key: A 2D index is a city map divided into
name: ch03_register_and_map_grid
alt: A register sorted by class then roll number makes one question easy and another hard, while a city map divided into squares lets you check only the squares you are viewing.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a school office where a clerk has a big register sorted first by class and then by roll number, with coloured tabs for each class sticking out of the edge; a teacher asks for one whole class and the clerk flips straight to one tab, a short easy arrow; a second teacher asks for roll number 12 from every class, and the clerk wearily turns every page from front to back, many little arrows marching through the whole book. RIGHT panel: a large city map spread out on a table, divided into a grid of squares like postal areas; a young couple in casual clothes hold a rectangular glass frame over the map that covers the area they are viewing on their phone, and only the four grid squares touching the frame are lit up, each holding small restaurant pin icons, while all other squares are dimmed and ignored. A small compass rose and a coffee cup sit at the map corner, and the couple look pleased at how few squares they need to check. Bright daylight. Labels: "CLASS, ROLL" on the register's spine, "GRID" over the city map.

key: Edit distance counts the fewest
name: ch03_typo_and_trie
alt: A phone keyboard corrects a misspelled word that is one swap away, and a branching dictionary index groups words that share their first letters.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a close-up of a young man's hands typing on a large smartphone keyboard while sitting on a bus; the text field shows a misspelled word with two letters crossed in the wrong order, highlighted with a wavy underline, and a suggestion bubble above the keyboard shows a small chair icon with the corrected word; a tiny curved swap arrow between the two letters shows they just need to change places, and a counter shows one or two fixes. RIGHT panel: an illustrated branching tree carved on a wooden board in a classroom, like a family tree for words, where a single first letter at the top splits into branches for second letters, then third letters, and word leaves hang at the ends; words that begin the same way share the same trunk and branches. A teacher in a sari points along one branch with a stick while a student copies it. Light, airy background. Labels: "EDIT DISTANCE" above the left panel, "TRIE" above the tree in the right panel.

key: looks them up in a ledger every time
name: ch03_shopkeeper_memory_vs_ledger
alt: One shopkeeper quotes prices from memory instantly while another, with the ledger already open, still goes through a slow lookup ritual; both note sales in a diary.
scene: Two neighbouring grocery counters side by side, divided by a thin vertical line, both with a customer asking the price of a packet of tea. LEFT counter: a sharp young shopkeeper in a striped shirt taps his temple with one finger and answers at once, a thought bubble above him showing a neat glowing price list; he jots the sale in a small pocket diary at his elbow. RIGHT counter: an older shopkeeper in a white vest has a big ledger already open right in front of him on the counter, yet he goes through a slow ritual shown as small numbered steps: licks his finger and flips pages, runs his finger down columns, squints at the page format, slips a bookmark in to hold his place; the customer drums her fingers. He too notes the sale in the same kind of pocket diary. A small clock over each counter shows the left answer is instant and the right one slow, even though the ledger is right there. Warm afternoon light, gentle comedy. Labels: "IN-MEMORY" above the left counter, "DISK ENGINE" above the right counter, "LOG" on the pocket diary.

key: one person, one query, but it reads
name: ch03_oltp_vs_olap_railway
alt: Millions of travellers each book one seat on their phones, while one railway official reads a mountain of records to answer a five-year question.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a crowd of many small figures, students, a farmer, an auntie, a businessman, each holding a phone showing one seat on a train coach diagram; each person taps once and a tiny quick lightning bolt flies from their phone to a single seat in a long row of coaches above them, and every bolt is short and fast. The mood is busy, many people, tiny actions. RIGHT panel: a quiet wood-panelled board room where one senior railway official in a grey suit and spectacles sits at a long table, surrounded by a towering mountain of paper records stacked to the ceiling, bundled by month and route; a big chart on an easel behind him shows tiny bars per route per month; he reads through the stacks with a magnifying glass while an assistant wheels in yet another trolley of records. A single wall clock shows the hours passing. Bright busy light on the left, calm lamp light on the right. Labels: "OLTP" above the left panel, "OLAP" above the right panel.

key: every night a clerk copies each register
name: ch03_school_etl_archive
alt: At night a school clerk copies the fee, library, sports and exam registers, fixes their formats and files them into one archive room the principal studies.
scene: A school building at night shown as a cut-away with three rooms left to right connected by a corridor. LEFT room: four separate offices side by side, a fee counter, a library desk, a sports store and an exam cell, each with its own register left on the desk, lights off. MIDDLE room: a diligent clerk in a sleeveless sweater works under a single desk lamp, pulling copies of the four registers onto his table; he is rewriting a class name written two different ways into one standard form, shown as two small cards merging into one card with a green tick; a wall clock shows midnight. RIGHT room: a large, tidy archive room with tall shelves and uniform labelled box files, where the clerk's assistant slides a new box onto the shelf. In a small inset at the top right, it is the next morning: the principal, a dignified woman in her 50s with a shawl, sits in the archive with a cup of tea, studying a trend chart made from the boxes, while the fee counter in the left room bustles with parents undisturbed. Labels: "EXTRACT" over the left room, "TRANSFORM" over the middle room, "LOAD" over the right room.

key: A hospital with one reception desk
name: ch03_hospital_two_departments
alt: One hospital reception desk sends patients to a fast emergency ward and research requests to a slow medical records room.
scene: A cut-away view of a hospital ground floor. In the centre front stands a single long reception desk with a friendly receptionist in a blue uniform and a headset, a plain sign over the desk showing a speech bubble icon. Behind the desk, the building splits into two very different wings. LEFT wing: a bright, fast emergency ward where a doctor and a nurse wheel one patient on a stretcher at speed, monitors beeping, a big clock showing minutes, only one patient handled at a time with swift arrows. RIGHT wing: a quiet, dim medical records room with rolling shelves of thousands of patient files; a research doctor in a white coat and glasses sits at a long table with stacks of folders and a magnifying glass, writing tallies; a trolley of more files is being wheeled in. Visitors at the desk include a man clutching his arm in pain, who gets pointed to the left wing, and a researcher with a clipboard, who gets pointed to the right wing. Clean hospital lighting. Labels: "SQL" over the reception desk, "OLTP" over the emergency wing, "OLAP" over the records room.

key: Row-at-a-time: an officer opens each
name: ch03_vote_tray_vectorized
alt: One counting officer handles ballots one at a time with many steps each, while a machine sweeps a whole tray of ballots at once through eight slots.
scene: A vote counting hall with long tables, split into two halves by a thin vertical line. LEFT half: a weary election officer in a white kurta and a lanyard opens one ballot box, unfolds a single ballot, checks it against a rule book, writes in a register, and only then reaches for the next box; small numbered step icons hover over each action, and a long queue of sealed ballot boxes stretches behind him. RIGHT half: a sturdy grey counting machine on a table takes in a whole tray of ballots stacked flat at once; a clear panel on its front shows eight identical slots, each holding one ballot, all being checked in a single sweep of a scanning bar, with a fan of eight short arrows coming out the other side into neat sorted piles. A young technician in a cap feeds the next tray. The left side feels slow and repetitive, the right fast and parallel. Bright overhead hall lights, dust motes. Labels: "ROW AT A TIME" above the left half, "VECTORIZED" above the right half, "SIMD" beside the eight-slot panel.

key: Three photocopies of the same class
name: ch03_three_sorted_copies
alt: Three teachers each hold a complete copy of the class register, sorted by roll number, by house and by bus route.
scene: A school corridor outside a classroom at the start of the day, seen from the front. Three teachers stand side by side, each holding a full photocopy of the same class register, but each copy visibly sorted in a different way. On the left, the class teacher in a sari holds a copy with rows in order of roll number, tiny numbers 1, 2, 3 in the margin. In the middle, the sports teacher in a tracksuit with a whistle holds a copy grouped by house, with coloured flag icons in red, blue, green and yellow along the margin. On the right, the bus in-charge in a cap and reflective vest holds a copy grouped by bus route, with small bus icons in the margin. Each teacher looks quickly and happily at their own copy. Behind them, the original register lies on a shelf, and a small inset shows one copy dropped in a puddle while the other two teachers still have everything. The students' photos on all three copies are the same faces in different orders. Bright morning light. Labels: "BY ROLL" over the left copy, "BY HOUSE" over the middle copy, "BY BUS" over the right copy.

key: So new sales go on a sticky-note pad
name: ch03_bound_report_sticky_notes
alt: A bound yearly sales report cannot take new lines, so new sales go on a sticky-note pad that readers check too, until the report is reprinted with the notes merged in.
scene: An office desk seen from slightly above. In the centre lies a thick, hard-bound yearly sales report with a ribbon bookmark, closed and solid, with a small padlock icon on its spine to show nothing can be squeezed into its pages.
