Stuck to the front cover is a pad of bright yellow sticky notes, the top few filled with short scribbled lines and tiny rupee icons for the newest sales. A manager in his 40s with rolled-up sleeves reads the bound report and the sticky notes together, one hand holding the book open and the other lifting a note, a dotted line joining the two to show he checks both. On the right side of the desk, a printer is pushing out the pages of a fresh new edition of the report, with the yellow notes visibly merged into its printed pages, and an empty sticky pad waiting next to it. A coffee cup, a stapler and a desk calendar with a ring around the year end complete the desk. Warm office light, organised mood. Labels: "SORTED" on the bound report, "NEW WRITES" on the sticky-note pad, "MERGE" over the printer.

key: some counters have the new printer
name: ch04_pnr_slip_new_line
alt: During a format change, a new counter reads an old ticket slip fine and an old counter reads a new slip by skipping the line it does not know.
scene: A railway reservation hall with two counters side by side, divided by a thin vertical line, during the weeks when a new ticket-slip format is being rolled out. LEFT counter: a shiny new counter with a modern printer and a fresh sticker; a young clerk in a crisp shirt reads an old-style ticket slip handed in by an elderly passenger in a dhoti, the slip having fewer printed lines, and the clerk nods comfortably with a green tick bubble over the slip. RIGHT counter: an older counter with a dusty beige printer; a middle-aged clerk with spectacles reads a new-style slip handed in by a college student; the slip has one extra highlighted line near the bottom with a small berth icon, and the clerk places a ruler over that line, skips it with a small hop arrow, and carries on reading the name and train number lines, which are circled in green. Neither clerk looks alarmed. On the wall between the counters hangs a calendar showing a few weeks marked as the change-over period. Warm tube-light glow, steady mood of a system that keeps working while it changes. Labels: "BACKWARD" over the left counter, "FORWARD" over the right counter.

key: Built-in formats are home-made jars
name: ch04_pickle_jar_language_formats
alt: A homemade pickle jar is perfect in the home kitchen but cannot be shipped abroad for a lab to identify, and a swapped jar hides unknown contents.
scene: A three-part scene, left to right, all built around one round glass pickle jar with a cloth tied over its mouth and a red handwritten label. LEFT part: a cosy home kitchen where a grandmother in a cotton sari spoons bright mango pickle onto a grandson's plate; everyone knows exactly what is inside, and the jar sits happily on the familiar shelf. MIDDLE part: the same jar in a cardboard box at an international customs desk; a foreign lab technician in a white coat and safety goggles holds it up to the light, puzzled, with a big question mark, because nothing on it tells a stranger what it contains. RIGHT part: a sneaky figure in a hood is swapping the jar on the kitchen shelf for an identical-looking jar, and in a small inset bubble that second jar is opened and a small mechanical spring-loaded gadget pops out instead of pickle, hinting that opening a jar can run something unexpected. A dotted path links the three parts so it reads as one jar's journey. Warm kitchen light on the left, cold official light in the middle, shadowy light on the right. Labels: "SAME KITCHEN" above the left part, "TRAVELS" above the middle part, "SWAPPED" above the right part.

key: The numbered columns are the field
name: ch04_scorebook_field_tags
alt: A cricket scorer writes only column numbers and values in a scorebook whose printed headings at the top say what each number means.
scene: Close-up of a cricket scorer's desk in a pavilion box. A large scorebook lies open, and the hero of the image is its layout: across the very top of the page is a printed header row where each column has a small number in a circle and a little icon, a bat for the batter, a running figure for runs, a ball for balls faced. Below, the rows are filled not with long words but with short entries: just a circled column number and a value, written quickly in pencil. The scorer, a lean man in his 60s with a white cap, spectacles and a pencil behind his ear, is writing one such short entry while glancing up at the field through the window, where a batter has just played a shot. A thin dotted line runs from one short entry up to the matching numbered heading to show that the number means the heading. On the side of the desk sits a second scorebook from another club with its header columns numbered in a different order, with a small warning triangle, to hint that the numbers only work while everyone agrees on them. Afternoon sunlight, cosy concentration. Labels: "TAG" beside a circled column number, "SCHEMA" over the printed header row.

key: Think of an old car odometer with only
name: ch04_odometer_truncation
alt: A long seven-digit distance reading is squeezed onto an old five-digit odometer, which silently shows a much smaller wrong number.
scene: A workshop scene in a small Indian garage. On the left, a modern hatchback with its dashboard lit up shows a seven-digit odometer reading with all digits clear. A thin glowing stream of digits flows out of that dashboard along a cable towards the right, where an old vintage car's round chrome odometer dial has room for only five digit windows. As the stream arrives, the first two digits hit the edge of the old dial and are clipped off, falling away like snipped paper and dropping into a small bin, while the last five digits slot neatly into the windows, showing a much smaller number. A mechanic in his 40s in grey overalls with a spanner in his pocket looks at the old dial, satisfied that nothing broke, completely unaware that the number is wrong. Behind him, the car's owner, a man in a checked shirt, looks at the small number and grins, thinking the car is nearly new. No sparks, no alarm, just a calm, silently wrong result. Warm garage light, oil cans on shelves. Labels: "7 DIGITS" above the modern dashboard, "5 DIGITS" above the old dial, "TRUNCATED" over the falling clipped digits.

key: A wedding RSVP form changed between
name: ch04_rsvp_card_schema_resolution
alt: A caterer copies answers from an old RSVP card to her new sheet by heading, dropping an unused field and filling a default for a new one.
scene: A wedding caterer's busy office table, seen from above. On the left lies an old printed RSVP card with three headed lines: a name line, a guests line with a family icon, and a meal line with a plate icon. On the right lies the caterer's new printed sheet with three headed columns in a different order: meal first, then name, then a phone column with a phone icon. The caterer, a smart woman in her 40s in a printed kurta with her hair tied back and reading glasses on her nose, copies the answers across with a pen. Curved arrows run from the old card to the new sheet, matched by headings rather than position, so the meal arrow crosses over the name arrow. The guests line on the old card has no arrow at all and is shown dropping lightly into a wastepaper basket. In the phone column on her sheet she writes a short dash with a small default stamp next to it. A pile of other old RSVP cards waits beside her, and a template card of the old format is pinned up on a corkboard behind her for reference. Bright daylight, marigold decorations on boxes. Labels: "WRITER" over the old card, "READER" over the new sheet, "DEFAULT" by the stamp.

key: old apps never send it, new apps fill
name: ch04_payment_form_optional_field
alt: Adding an optional note box to a payment form is harmless for old records, but a new compulsory box with no default rejects them.
scene: A split-panel illustration of a payments office archive, divided by a thin vertical line, each half showing a large payment form template on an easel and a filing cabinet of old payment slips beside it. LEFT panel: the new form template has an extra box at the bottom with a soft dashed border and a tiny feather icon meaning optional, already pre-filled with a blank default; a friendly clerk in a cardigan feeds old slips from the cabinet into a reading machine, and every slip comes out the other side with a green tick, the new box simply shown empty. RIGHT panel: the new form template has a heavy solid red-bordered box marked with a small padlock icon meaning compulsory and no default; the same clerk feeds an old slip into the machine, and the machine spits it back out with a red cross and a puff of smoke, a growing pile of rejected old slips on the floor; the clerk scratches his head because the old slips can never be asked for the missing value. Neutral office light, clear before-and-after contrast. Labels: "OPTIONAL" over the left form's new box, "REQUIRED" over the right form's new box.

key: A big ledger book: the column headings
name: ch04_three_ways_to_share_schema
alt: Three ways to share a format: headings printed once in a ledger, a drawer of version-stamped receipts with a reference binder, and two callers agreeing on a language first.
scene: A three-panel picture, read left to right, in a traditional trading office. PANEL ONE: a huge ledger book open on a desk, with the column headings printed once in bold on the first page only, while dozens of later pages hold rows of plain values; a thin ribbon bookmark links later pages back to the headings page. PANEL TWO: a wooden drawer pulled open, full of loose paper receipts from many years, each with a small round version stamp in a corner showing a number; beside the drawer stands a thick ring binder opened to a page that shows the layout of each version, and a young accountant in a shirt matches a receipt's stamp number to a binder page. PANEL THREE: two people on landline phones in two different cities, a shopkeeper and a supplier, both saying the first sentence of the call as a speech bubble showing a small language flag icon with a handshake symbol between the bubbles, agreeing on one language before talking business. A thin connecting band along the bottom unites the three panels as three answers to the same question. Warm wood office light. Labels: "FILE" above panel one, "VERSION" above panel two, "NEGOTIATE" above panel three.

key: Codegen is a pre-printed form with boxes
name: ch04_form_vs_letter_codegen
alt: A strict office checks every box on a pre-printed form, while a friend simply reads a letter that explains itself.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a strict government office with a counter and a tall stack of files; a stern officer in a grey safari suit and spectacles inspects a pre-printed form with neat boxes, one box per field, ticking every box with a red pen and a ruler; an applicant in a formal shirt waits nervously, and a box left empty glows red before the form even leaves the counter, showing mistakes are caught early. RIGHT panel: a sunny verandah where a cheerful woman in a cotton salwar suit sits on a cane chair reading a handwritten letter from a friend, the letter itself beginning with a small heading that says what each paragraph is about, shown as tiny icons at the start of each paragraph; she reads it freely without any form; in a small inset at the corner, later, she frowns at one paragraph that turned out to be about something else, showing a mistake caught only while reading. Office tube-light on the left, warm sunlight on the right. Labels: "CODEGEN" above the left panel, "DYNAMIC" above the right panel.

key: A schema is the official railway
name: ch04_timetable_schema
alt: An official railway timetable board is compact, always current and checked for clashes before a new one takes effect.
scene: A big railway station concourse with a giant official timetable board on the wall, compact rows of train numbers and times rather than long descriptions. In front of it, three vignettes. On the left, a passenger in a sweater compares the train number on his ticket with a row on the board and the train itself pulling into the platform behind, with matching numbers on its side, to show the trains literally run by the board. In the middle, a printed draft of next month's timetable lies on a planning table where two railway planners in white shirts, one older and one younger, run a ruler down it and circle a clash in red where two trains are assigned the same platform at the same time, catching the problem before the new board goes up. On the right, a worker on a tall ladder replaces a row of the board with a freshly printed strip, carefully, after the planners' approval stamp. A compact feel overall: numbers, not prose. Bright morning light from high windows, pigeons on the beams. Labels: "SCHEMA" above the timetable board, "CHECKED" by the circled clash on the planning table.

key: Three ways to get a message to your
name: ch04_message_three_ways
alt: A message reaches a brother three ways: written in a family diary for later, a phone call answered now, and a family chat group that delivers soon without waiting.
scene: A three-panel scene in an Indian home and a hostel, joined by the same young woman in a yellow kurta in each panel. PANEL ONE: she writes a note in a thick family diary that lies on a hall table beside a small brass lamp; an inset clock shows days passing, and her younger brother finds and reads it much later, still in his school uniform but with a calendar on the wall jumped forward. PANEL TWO: she holds a phone to her ear, and her brother in his hostel room answers at once, both speaking live, a straight line between the two phones with a small lightning icon. PANEL THREE: she taps a message into a family chat group on her phone; a speech bubble flies into a cloud-shaped group icon and then out to several phones, the brother's, a cousin's, the mother's, each getting it a little later; she is already putting her phone away and walking off to the kitchen, not waiting for any reply. Bright daylight, homely mood. Labels: "DATABASE" above panel one, "RPC" above panel two, "MESSAGE BROKER" above panel three.

key: updates the family address register
name: ch04_lost_field_old_form
alt: A mother copies family entries onto last year's printed form, which has no email column, so the sister's added email silently disappears.
scene: A dining table at home, seen from above, in the afternoon. On the left lies the current family address register page, where an entry for the son has three filled columns: a name, a phone number being corrected, and an extra email column that the sister added in her own handwriting with a small envelope icon. On the right lies a stack of printed forms from last year, with only two columns, name and phone, and no email column at all. The mother, a kind woman in her 50s in a cotton sari with reading glasses, copies the entry carefully onto one of last year's forms, fixing the phone number with a smile. A dotted arrow carries the name and the new phone across into the form, while the email, drawn as a little envelope, falls off the edge of the table into empty air, unnoticed by anyone. In the background, the sister in a college hoodie walks into the room, reading her phone, not yet aware her email is gone. Warm, calm home light; the loss is quiet, not dramatic. Labels: "OLD FORM" on the printed form stack, "LOST" next to the falling envelope.

key: photos from 1985 are black-and-white
name: ch04_family_album_eras
alt: A family album holds black-and-white prints, colour prints and phone printouts side by side, none reprinted, all fitting the same slots.
scene: A family sitting on a sofa looking through a big old cloth-bound photo album opened across three laps, seen from the front. The open album pages are the hero of the image: in one row of slots sit three kinds of photos from different decades, a small black-and-white print with scalloped white edges showing young grandparents at their wedding, a bright colour print showing parents with a baby at a beach, and a glossy phone printout of a grandchild blowing out birthday candles. Each photo fits into identical photo-corner slots on the page, none of them reprinted to match the others. A small handwritten year tag sits under each slot. On the sofa, the grandmother in a white sari points at the old print, the father in a polo shirt holds the album steady, and a teenage girl in a hoodie smiles at the newest print. On the coffee table lies an old film camera, a compact digital camera and a smartphone in a row, showing how the camera changed while the album stayed the same. Warm evening lamp light, nostalgic mood. Labels: "1985", "2005" and "2024" as the year tags under the three photos.

key: Scanning your old school certificates
name: ch04_certificates_scan_archive
alt: Old certificates of different sizes and styles go through a scanner and come out as one consistent bound archive file.
scene: A home study desk with a flatbed scanner in the middle. On the left of the scanner sits a messy pile of old school certificates and mark sheets of all different shapes and paper: a small yellowed primary school certificate with a ribbon seal, a long sports certificate with a gold border, a typed mark sheet on thin blue paper, a handwritten character certificate. A young man in his 20s in a T-shirt, sitting on a desk chair, feeds them one by one into the scanner. On the right of the scanner a clean, uniform stack of identical-sized digital pages floats out like cards, all the same size and style, and goes into a neat locked folder icon on the laptop screen beside it, with a small padlock to show the archive is not edited afterwards. One scanned card shows a small blank field filled in with a default dash because the oldest certificate never had that field. A cup of tea and a stapler sit on the desk. Afternoon window light. Labels: "MIXED" over the old pile, "ARCHIVE" over the uniform stack on the right.

key: calls the order service, which itself
name: ch04_food_order_microservices
alt: A food order from a phone fans out from an order team to separate restaurant, payment and delivery teams, each running on its own schedule.
scene: A tall open-plan office building drawn as a cut-away with several separate rooms, like a dollhouse. At the bottom left, a hungry young man on a sofa at home taps an order on his phone; a glowing envelope flies from the phone up into the first room, where a small team with a sign showing a receipt icon receives it. From that room three more envelopes fly out to three other rooms: a room with a chef-hat sign where a team checks a restaurant kitchen's status, a room with a rupee sign where a team handles a payment, and a room with a scooter sign where a team assigns a delivery rider shown on a map. Each room has its own wall calendar with different release dates circled and its own small rocket icon on a different launch day, showing each team ships on its own schedule. One of the envelopes is a slightly different colour and shape, to hint it was written by a newer version of a team. People in each room wear different coloured lanyards. Bright office light, busy friendly mood. Labels: "CLIENT" by the man on the sofa, "SERVICES" across the row of team rooms.

key: REST is the railway enquiry counter
name: ch04_rest_vs_soap_counters
alt: Anyone can walk up to a simple enquiry counter with a train number, while a formal office requires triplicate forms and a special clerk.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a simple open railway enquiry window with a cheerful clerk in a white shirt; a short line of very different people, a college student, a farmer with a cloth bag and a businessman with a briefcase, each just says a train number and gets a quick answer slip, with a big friendly sign above showing a question mark and a train icon. The counter has no forms, just a small bell. RIGHT panel: a formal government office with a high wooden counter, stacks of files tied with red tape and a carbon-paper pad; an applicant in a formal suit holds a thick form printed in triplicate, white, pink and yellow sheets, and waits for a particular senior clerk who sits behind a nameplate showing only a stamp icon; a rule book lies open next to him and a special stamp machine sits on the desk. Everything on the right is precise but needs the right papers and the right person. Bright on the left, dim and dusty on the right. Labels: "REST" above the left panel, "SOAP" above the right panel.

key: Getting a home loan: you need a salary
name: ch04_home_loan_futures
alt: Instead of visiting three offices one after another, a loan applicant sends three helpers at once and combines their papers when the slowest returns.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a single tired man in his 30s in a formal shirt walks a long winding road through a town, visiting three offices one after another, an office with a payslip sign, a bank with a statement sign and a tax office with a card sign, a sun moving across the sky from morning to afternoon above him, sweat on his brow. RIGHT panel: the same man sits calmly at a cafe table with a cup of tea; three helpers, his younger sister, a cousin and a friend, have each been sent at the same moment to the three offices along three parallel roads, and are now walking back with papers; two have already returned and handed papers over, and the third is just arriving, and a small clock above him shows the total wait equals the slowest helper. One helper holds a paper with a small red cross icon, hinting that any errand can fail, so the combined file must cope with a missing paper. Bright midday light. Labels: "ONE BY ONE" above the left panel, "FUTURES" above the right panel.

key: It first upgrades every machine in the
name: ch04_cheque_machine_upgrade
alt: A bank first upgrades all cheque machines to accept both old and new cheque books, then mails new books, while old-book customers keep working.
scene: A two-step scene inside a bank clearing house and a residential street, read left to right with a big step-1 and step-2 arrow between them. STEP ONE, left: inside a clearing house, technicians in blue overalls upgrade a long row of cheque-processing machines; each upgraded machine has two input slots, one shaped for an old-style cheque and one shaped for a new-style cheque with an extra printed strip, and both slots glow green. STEP TWO, right: a postman on a bicycle delivers fresh new cheque books to houses on a residential street, while an elderly customer in a shawl still hands an old-style cheque book to a bank teller, and the machine accepts it happily. A receipt slip coming out of a machine has one extra new line at the bottom, and the elderly customer reads only the familiar top lines and ignores the new one, shown with a small dotted line skipping past it. Calm, orderly, practical mood with warm daylight. Labels: "SERVERS FIRST" over the clearing house, "CLIENTS LATER" over the street, "IGNORED" by the new line on the receipt.

key: each cook (actor) has an order-slip
name: ch04_kitchen_actors
alt: In a big kitchen each cook works from his own slip tray without touching others' pans, slips sometimes fall, and a runner carries slips to a second kitchen across the road.
scene: A large busy restaurant kitchen seen from above at an angle, with a row of cooking stations. Each station has one cook in a white uniform and cap, and in front of each cook is a small metal tray holding a short pile of paper order slips; each cook picks up just one slip at a time and works on it at his own pan, and nobody reaches into another cook's pan; small dashed boundaries around each station show the separation. Waiters drop new slips into specific trays. One slip has slipped off a tray and drifted to the floor, and nearby cooks glance at it without panic, used to it happening. On the right side, through an open door, a road with a second kitchen across it is visible; a young runner in a cap jogs across the road with a handful of slips, delivering them into a tray of a cook in the second kitchen, who works exactly the same way. Steam, flame and clatter drawn as small squiggles. Warm kitchen light, busy but calm mood. Labels: "ACTOR" over one cook's station, "MESSAGE" on a slip in a tray, "RUNNER" over the person crossing the road.

key: A single chai stall at a railway station
name: ch05_chai_counters_platforms
alt: A station chai business adds counters for crowds, a second tea-maker for sickness, and a counter on a far platform so nobody crosses the bridge.
scene: A wide view of a busy Indian railway station from above, with a long footbridge crossing several platforms. Three small vignettes are arranged along the platforms. On platform 1, a chai counter that used to be one stall now has three identical counters side by side, each pouring tea for a separate short queue of passengers, to show more counters for a bigger crowd. Next to them, behind one counter, one tea-maker in a vest sits on a stool with a thermometer in his mouth and a shawl over his shoulders looking unwell, while a second tea-maker in an identical apron cheerfully keeps pouring, so service never stops. Far away on platform 8, a brand-new matching counter serves passengers stepping off a just-arrived train, and a thin dotted line shows the long walk over the footbridge that those passengers no longer need to make, with a small crossed-out walking figure on the bridge. All counters share the same striped awning and the same kettle design, clearly copies of one stall. Morning light, steam rising from every kettle, cheerful bustle. Labels: "MORE COUNTERS" over platform 1, "BACKUP" over the second tea-maker, "NEARBY" over the platform 8 counter.

key: replacing your autorickshaw with a bus
name: ch05_scale_up_and_shared_pump
alt: A driver upgrades from an autorickshaw to ever bigger buses that cost more and still break in one place, and several drivers queue at one shared fuel pump.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a road going uphill from left to right like steps, with a three-wheeled autorickshaw at the bottom, then a minibus, then a big bus, then an enormous double-length bus at the top; each vehicle has a price tag hanging from its mirror, the tags growing much larger with each step; the same driver, a moustached man in a khaki uniform, sits proudly in each one; at the very top the giant bus has broken down with steam pouring from its bonnet and every passenger stuck inside, showing one big machine still fails in one place. RIGHT panel: a single petrol pump at a roadside station, with a queue of several autorickshaws and small vans lined up, each driver leaning out of the window waiting impatiently; only one vehicle can be fuelled at a time, and the pump attendant waves the next one forward while the others idle, small exhaust puffs above each. Afternoon light, dusty road. Labels: "SCALE UP" above the left panel, "SHARED DISK" above the pump in the right panel.

key: A franchise of kirana shops. Each shop
name: ch05_kirana_franchise_shared_nothing
alt: A row of franchise kirana shops, each with its own shopkeeper, counter and storeroom, coordinate by phone; one flooded shop does not close the others.
scene: A street view of four identical small kirana shops in a row along a town road, each painted in the same colours with the same awning. Each shop is cut away to show its own three parts: a shopkeeper at the counter, a busy counter top with a weighing scale and a notepad, and a small storeroom at the back stacked with sacks and cartons. The shopkeepers are different people, a young woman in a salwar suit, an old man in a white kurta, a middle-aged man in a vest, a young man in a T-shirt, and each is talking on a landline phone; a thin telephone wire runs overhead from shop to shop, linking all four. The second shop from the right is flooded with knee-deep rainwater, its shopkeeper standing on a stool holding a phone and waving, while the other three shops are dry and serving customers normally. At the far right, a worker is painting the signboard of a fifth matching shop that is just opening. Monsoon clouds on the right, sunlight on the left. Labels: "OWN STOREROOM" over one storeroom, "PHONE LINE" along the overhead wire.

key: a 2-volume encyclopaedia. Partitioning
name: ch05_encyclopaedia_volumes
alt: A school library splits an encyclopaedia into two volumes on two shelves, and keeps two copies of each volume so a lost copy does not matter.
scene: A bright school library with wooden shelves and long reading tables. On the left wall is a shelf labelled with a small A-to-M plaque holding two identical red encyclopaedia volumes side by side; on the right wall is a shelf with an N-to-Z plaque holding two identical blue encyclopaedia volumes side by side. A thick dashed line between the two shelves shows the split of the alphabet across volumes. On the left shelf, one of the two red volumes is missing, an empty gap with a dust outline, and a sticky note shows a small sad face; but at the table in front of it, a schoolgirl in a uniform with two plaits happily reads the other red copy, a page about an animal starting with a letter from the first half of the alphabet. A cheerful librarian in a sari and spectacles stands between the shelves pointing at both pairs of books, and a small boy at the right reads one of the blue copies. Sunbeams through tall windows, dust motes, calm study mood. Labels: "PARTITION" across the dashed dividing line, "REPLICA" over the pair of matching copies on the right shelf.

key: Photocopying a printed timetable for ten
name: ch05_changing_timetable_copies
alt: A timetable that changes every few minutes must reach ten stations by courier and fax, and one station is stuck with an old copy.
scene: A map-like scene of a railway line with ten small stations strung along it like beads, seen from above. At the central head office on the left, a busy clerk in a white shirt stands next to a photocopier as it pushes out yet another fresh timetable, while a wall clock shows only minutes between versions, and small version numbers float above a growing pile of copies. From the head office, couriers on bicycles and a few fax lines carry copies out to the stations. Most stations have a station master pinning up the newest copy on a notice board with a green tick. But one courier has a flat tyre by the roadside, scratching his head, and one station's fax machine is smoking with a broken paper jam; at that station, an older station master is still reading an out-of-date timetable on his board, unaware, and a train is pulling in at a time that doesn't match his copy. Bright daylight, sense of constant change. Labels: "LATEST" over the head office pile, "STALE" over the station with the old copy.

key: Leader failover is the captain getting
name: ch05_captain_failover_split_brain
alt: An injured captain is replaced by the vice-captain, and when the old captain walks back on, both start setting the field at once.
scene: A cricket ground shown in three moments, left to right, joined by the same green outfield. LEFT moment: the team captain, a tall man with a captain's armband, lies on the grass holding his knee while two umpires in white coats and wide hats look at their watches, waiting to be sure he really cannot continue, a small timer icon above them. MIDDLE moment: the vice-captain, a younger player with a clipboard field plan tucked under his arm, steps forward with the armband now on his sleeve, and all the fielders turn to face him, small arrows from each fielder pointing to him for signals. RIGHT moment: the original captain, now bandaged, jogs back onto the field waving his arms and pointing fielders one way, while the vice-captain points them the other way; confused fielders stand between them, some running left and some right, two of them colliding. A small inset at the top corner shows a schoolboy back from sick leave handing a friend a notebook open at a dated page, asking for everything after it. Bright afternoon sun, stadium crowd in the background. Labels: "FAILOVER" over the middle moment, "SPLIT BRAIN" over the right moment.

key: Statement: send the recipe card
name: ch05_second_kitchen_methods
alt: Four ways to make a second kitchen copy the first: send the recipe card, a precise burner-level record, the finished result, or a runner with a register.
scene: A four-panel grid showing two side-by-side kitchens in every panel, the main kitchen on the left and a second kitchen on the right, with something being passed between them. TOP LEFT: a cook hands a recipe card through a hatch to a second cook, who tastes from a spoon with a doubtful face, because the card just says to taste. TOP RIGHT: a precise printout like a security camera log with tiny burner numbers and time stamps is passed over, and the second kitchen's stove has the same four burners in the same positions, so the second cook matches it exactly. BOTTOM LEFT: a finished bowl of dal on a tray with a tag showing a table number and a small volume mark is passed over, and the second kitchen, which has a different stove layout, simply reproduces that same bowl. BOTTOM RIGHT: a waiter writes each order into a register, and a runner carries the register across the yard to the second kitchen, crossing out one line and translating another on the way with a pencil. Warm kitchen light, steam everywhere. Labels: "STATEMENT" above the top-left panel, "WAL" above the top-right panel, "LOGICAL" above the bottom-left panel; the runner panel stays unlabelled.

key: Wait until everyone is out of the tunnel
name: ch05_phone_in_tunnel
alt: A sent message has reached some friends but not one whose train is in a tunnel, so two friends asked at once give different answers.
scene: A wide landscape scene. On the left, a young man in a hoodie sits at a cafe table and has just sent a message from his phone; a speech-bubble icon with two small ticks flies out across the picture. In the middle, a hilly landscape with a railway track entering a dark tunnel; a train is half inside the tunnel, and through one window we see a friend holding a phone with a spinning loading icon and no signal bars, the message bubble hovering just outside the tunnel mouth, waiting. On the right, in a bright city square, two other friends stand side by side holding their phones; a curious aunt between them asks what he said; one friend's phone shows the message bubble and she answers confidently, while the other friend's phone shows an older conversation and he shrugs with a different answer. A small inset at the far right shows the train out of the tunnel and all three phones showing the same message, everyone nodding. Daylight, soft clouds. Labels: "SENT" by the young man's phone, "LAGGING" over the tunnel, "EVENTUALLY" over the small inset.

key: App 1 says India 150/3. You refresh
name: ch05_score_goes_backwards
alt: A cricket fan refreshes and switches to a lagging score app, so a wicket seems to un-fall, while another fan sticking to one app sees the score only move forward.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing a cricket fan on a living-room sofa with a phone during a big match. LEFT panel: a young man in a team jersey holds his phone; a first screen shows a higher score with three wickets, and after a swipe-to-refresh arrow, a second screen from a different app shows a lower score with only two wickets; a fallen wicket icon floats back up into the air like it has un-fallen, and the man's jaw drops in confusion, his popcorn spilling. RIGHT panel: his sister in the same kind of jersey keeps using one app only; she refreshes several times and the screens show the score creeping forward one step at a time, a little behind the live action on the TV in the background, but never going backwards, a small forward-only arrow under her screens. She munches calmly. A small TV on the wall in both panels shows the real live match. Evening living-room lamp light. Labels: "150/3" on the first left screen, "142/2" on the second left screen, "MONOTONIC" above the right panel.

key: A family WhatsApp group where Papa asks
name: ch05_reply_before_question
alt: On a phone in a family chat group, a sister's reply arrives before her father's question, leaving the reader confused.
scene: A family scene shown as a cut-away of three homes connected by dotted signal lines. In the left home, a father in his 50s in a sleeveless sweater types a question into a family chat group on his phone, a thought bubble showing a grandmother with a suitcase at a railway station. In the right home, his daughter in a college hoodie quickly replies with a raised hand and a clock showing six. In the middle home, a young son on a bed looks at his own phone: the hero of the image is his screen, enlarged in a bubble above him, where the daughter's reply bubble with the raised hand and clock appears first and the father's question bubble is still a grey loading placeholder below it. The dotted line from the father's home to the son's phone takes a long, looping, slow route around a hill, while the daughter's line goes straight and short. The son scratches his head with a puzzled look. Evening light through windows. Labels: "ANSWER" on the first bubble, "QUESTION" on the grey loading bubble, "OUT OF ORDER" above the son.

key: phone is off for three days
name: ch05_wedding_planner_slow_reply
alt: A wedding planner tracks replies from relatives, most arriving in a minute, while one uncle's phone is off for three days and she has a backup plan.
scene: A wedding planner's home office, decorated with fabric swatches and marigold samples. A capable woman in her 30s in a bright saree and a headset sits at a desk with a big wall chart of relatives' names, each with a reply tick and a time; most ticks are green and show a quick reply within a minute. Floating on the right, a series of phones of relatives, an aunt, a cousin, a grandfather, all lit up with quick reply ticks. One phone in the series belongs to an uncle in a cap who is shown dozing on a train berth in a far-away hill village, his phone in a bag with a dead battery icon and a calendar beside him with three days crossed. On the wall chart, his row has a small hourglass. The planner is not panicking: she points to a second, smaller backup plan sheet pinned next to the chart that shows three options as icons, a detour arrow, an hourglass and a stop hand. Bright, organised, festive mood. Labels: "FAST REPLIES" over the lit phones, "3 DAYS" by the dozing uncle, "PLAN B" on the backup sheet.

key: shared expense notebook, but Papa keeps
name: ch05_two_expense_notebooks
alt: A father at home and an uncle at his shop each keep a copy of the family expense notebook and swap new entries every evening, sometimes writing the same bill twice.
scene: A split scene of two places joined in the middle. LEFT: a home living room where a father in his 50s in a kurta and reading glasses writes in a ruled expense notebook on a side table. RIGHT: a small cloth shop where his younger brother, an uncle with a moustache in a striped shirt, writes in an identical notebook on his counter between rolls of fabric. Both notebooks have the same cover. In the middle, an evening sky with a crescent moon, and two dotted arrows looping between the notebooks in both directions carrying small paper slips of new entries, showing the evening exchange. Close-ups of the two open notebooks show both men have written the same entry for an electricity bill with a light-bulb icon for the same month, each on their own copy; a small red clash spark appears where the two arrows cross over that entry. Both men glance up thoughtfully from their notebooks. Warm lamp light at home, tube light in the shop. Labels: "LEADER 1" over the father's notebook, "LEADER 2" over the uncle's notebook, "CONFLICT" by the clash spark.

key: A bank with branches in Mumbai and New
name: ch05_bank_branches_multi_leader
alt: With one leader, every distant deposit waits for approval across the ocean; with multi-leader, each branch updates its own ledger and they exchange ledgers overnight.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, each panel showing an Indian bank branch on the left and a foreign skyline branch on the right across a stylised ocean. LEFT panel: a customer in the Indian branch hands cash to a teller, who must pick up a heavy old telephone and wait for approval from a manager across the ocean; the phone cable stretches long over the waves and is snapped in the middle with a spark, the teller holding the dead receiver while a queue grows behind the customer. RIGHT panel: each branch has its own teller writing directly in its own ledger and serving customers at once; at night, under a moon, a small boat carries the two ledgers' new pages across the ocean in both directions; in a small inset, one account shows two different balances in the two ledgers with a red exclamation mark, hinting that both branches debited it on the same day. Daylight on the branches, night over the ocean. Labels: "SINGLE LEADER" above the left panel, "MULTI-LEADER" above the right panel.

key: kept by two teachers on a school trip
name: ch05_school_trip_registers
alt: Two teachers in two buses mark attendance in separate registers with no phone signal, then merge them at school and find one student marked differently.
scene: A split scene in two parts. TOP part: a winding hill road with two school buses driving one behind the other through pine trees and mist; a small phone icon with a red cross shows there is no signal. Inside each bus, cut away, a teacher holds a paper attendance register on her lap and ticks students as they board; the first teacher is a young woman in a cardigan, the second an older woman in a cotton sari with spectacles. TOP RIGHT, a boy with a cap is shown boarding the second bus late, holding a packet of chips. BOTTOM part: back in the school staff room, both teachers sit at one table with their two registers open side by side, running their fingers down matching rows and copying ticks into a single merged register; most rows match with green ticks, but one row, for the boy with the cap, shows a cross in one register and a tick in the other, and both teachers look at each other, needing to decide. A thin arrow leads from the buses down to the staff room table. Cool misty light above, warm room light below. Labels: "OFFLINE" over the buses, "MERGE" over the staff room table.

key: each family member edits only their own
name: ch05_family_diary_own_pages
alt: Each family member writes only on their own page of a shared diary, until a sister travels and her brother takes over her page, and both write on it the same day.
scene: A big family diary lying open on a dining table, seen from above, with clearly separated pages, each page having a small photo-corner portrait of its owner at the top: a father, a mother, a sister and a brother. LEFT half of the image: a peaceful routine where each family member sits at the table writing only on their own page, little dotted borders around each page, no elbows crossing. RIGHT half of the image: the sister, in a travel jacket with a backpack and a boarding pass, waves goodbye at the door, and the brother, a teenager in a T-shirt, has slid her page over to his side and is writing on it; but in a small inset bubble, the sister sits in a hill-station hotel room writing on a digital copy of the same page on her tablet at the same moment, and two overlapping lines of handwriting clash on her page with a small red spark. Warm home lighting on the left, cool travel light in the inset. Labels: "OWN PAGE" over the peaceful half, "SWAPPED" over the brother writing on his sister's page.

key: a collage of both. Record the conflict
name: ch05_display_picture_conflict
alt: Two cousins change a family group's picture at the same moment, shown with four ways to resolve it: latest clock wins, elder wins, a collage, or the admin chooses.
scene: A central scene with two cousins in different cities, a young woman on a balcony and a young man on a college bench, both tapping change-picture on their phones at the same instant, one uploading a beach photo and the other a mountain photo, two arrows flying into a single round group picture frame in the middle with a clash spark. Around the frame, four small outcome cards are arranged at the four corners. TOP LEFT: only the mountain photo remains, a clock icon shows a slightly later time stamp, and the beach photo is falling into a bin. TOP RIGHT: only the beach photo remains because a crown icon shows the elder cousin always wins. BOTTOM LEFT: the frame shows a collage of the beach and the mountain side by side. BOTTOM RIGHT: a grandmother acting as group admin holds her phone showing both photos with a pick-one prompt and a thoughtful finger on her chin. Bright, playful composition built around phone screens on a clean background. Labels: "LAST WRITE WINS" on the top-left card, "MERGE" on the bottom-left card, "ASK ADMIN" on the bottom-right card.

key: Two receptionists at two branches of
name: ch05_marriage_hall_double_booking
alt: Two receptionists at two branches each see a marriage hall free for the same date and book it for different families.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both panels showing a reception desk of a marriage hall company, each in a different town but with matching uniforms and the same logo-free wall sign showing a hall icon. LEFT panel: a cheerful receptionist in a maroon blazer smiles and shakes hands with a family of a bride's parents, while writing their name in her own copy of the booking register; a calendar on her desk shows one date circled in green, the hall shown free. RIGHT panel: a second receptionist in the same maroon blazer smiles and shakes hands with a different family, a groom's grandparents, writing their name for the same circled date in her own copy of the register. Above both panels, floating in the middle, a single picture of the actual hall with one stage and one wedding mandap, and two wedding processions with horses and bands arriving at its gate from opposite sides, about to meet with surprised faces. Bright, festive light. Labels: "HALL A" above the floating hall, "SAME DATE" next to both circled calendars.

key: News spreading in a family. Circular
name: ch05_family_news_topologies
alt: Family news spreads in a circle, through one grandmother at the centre, or with everyone calling everyone, each with its own weak spot.
scene: A three-panel illustration, each panel showing five or six relatives as portrait circles connected by phone call lines. PANEL ONE: the relatives sit in a ring, each line going only to the next person clockwise; one aunt in the ring is shown on a pilgrimage with a temple in the background and her phone switched off with a crossed icon, and the lines after her are greyed out, so two relatives further around look puzzled, never hearing the news. PANEL TWO: a grandmother sits in the centre with a big landline phone, every line running to her like spokes of a wheel; her phone is off while she naps on a chair, so every spoke is grey and everyone around her looks lost. PANEL THREE: every relative is connected to every other relative by lines in a web; one phone is off but the news still flows around it; however, one uncle gets a bubble showing a baby walking before he got the earlier bubble showing a baby being born, and looks bewildered. Small tag icons on the messages show who has already passed each one on. Warm, gentle colours. Labels: "CIRCULAR", "STAR" and "ALL-TO-ALL" each above its own panel.

key: every student hands their homework to
name: ch05_homework_to_any_teachers
alt: Instead of one class monitor collecting homework, each student hands copies to any three of five teachers, with no single person deciding the order.
scene: A school corridor with five teachers standing in a row at small desks, each with a tray for homework: a maths teacher in a sweater, a science teacher in a lab coat, an English teacher in a sari, a history teacher with a beard and a sports teacher in a tracksuit. A crowd of students in blue uniforms comes towards them, and each student holds three photocopies of the same homework and drops them into any three of the five trays, shown by thin arrows fanning out from each student to three different desks. The arrows from different students land on different combinations of desks, so each tray ends up with a slightly different pile. In a faded inset at the top left, the old way: a single class monitor with a badge collects all the homework in one pile and carries it to one teacher, with a crossed-out mark over the inset. At the far end, two teachers compare their piles and notice one tray is missing a sheet. Morning light through corridor windows. Labels: "LEADERLESS" above the row of teachers, "ANY THREE" above a student's fan of arrows.

key: Three dabbawalas keep a copy of the
name: ch05_delivery_lists_read_repair
alt: Three tiffin carriers compare delivery lists on a delivery and fix one outdated address on the spot, and a supervisor checks all lists line by line every Sunday.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a busy city pavement at noon where three tiffin carriers in white caps and kurtas meet before a delivery, each holding a small paper delivery list; they hold their lists side by side, and one carrier, who looks a little sunburnt from a recent holiday, has an old address on his list for one customer, drawn as an older building icon, while the other two lists show a new building icon; the other carriers point it out and he corrects it with a pencil right there on the pavement, a green tick appearing. RIGHT panel: a quiet Sunday afternoon in a small office, where a supervisor in a crisp white kurta and spectacles lays all three lists flat on a desk and runs a long ruler line by line down all of them at once, circling a difference for a customer who orders only once a year, shown as a small birthday-cake icon next to that line. A calendar on the wall shows Sunday. Sunlit street on the left, calm indoor light on the right. Labels: "READ REPAIR" above the left panel, "ANTI-ENTROPY" above the right panel.

key: Sloppy quorum: the neighbour signs for
name: ch05_neighbour_hinted_handoff
alt: With the flat locked, a courier leaves a parcel with a neighbour who notes it is for flat 302 and hands it over later, while the mother calling the flat hears it has not come.
scene: An apartment corridor on the third floor, seen from the end of the hallway, shown as a short sequence. On the left, a courier in a brown uniform holding a parcel stands at a locked door with a padlock on the latch; in a faded inset beside him, a version of the same courier walks away with the parcel back to his van, labelled as the strict choice. In the centre, a friendly neighbour, a retired man in a vest and spectacles, signs for the parcel at his own open door next door and sticks a small yellow note on it with a short flat number written on it. On the right, in the evening, the young woman who owns the flat, in office clothes with a laptop bag, receives the parcel from the neighbour with a smile. Floating above the corridor in a speech bubble, her mother calls the flat's landline from far away asking about the parcel, and the bubble from the flat's empty phone shows a shrug and a no, because the parcel is still next door at that moment. Warm corridor lights. Labels: "HINT" on the yellow note, "HANDOFF" over the evening moment, "302" on the locked door.

key: each stick a note on the fridge, at the
name: ch05_fridge_notes_lww
alt: Two flatmates stick errand notes on the fridge at the same moment, and a rule keeps only the note with the later time, silently binning the other.
scene: A small shared flat kitchen with a white fridge in the centre, seen straight on. From the left doorway, a young woman in a hoodie sticks a note with a milk-bottle icon onto the fridge door; from the right doorway, a young man in a T-shirt sticks a note with a bread-loaf icon onto the fridge door at exactly the same moment, both reaching in with outstretched arms. Each note has a small clock drawn in its corner, the times just a few minutes apart. Above the fridge, a magnetic rule card shows a clock icon with an arrow and a crown, meaning the later time wins. A third tidy-minded hand reaches in from above and drops the milk note into a pedal bin next to the fridge, leaving only the bread note on the door.
